payload.title: Creation of the world and of humankind

aliases: the God of our Lord Jesus Christ
him who sits on the throne
payload.name: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel
payload.note: The one God, creator and speaker of the Old Testament and the Father of Jesus Christ in the New Testament; distinct from Jesus in every entry.

stages.label: God the Father (radiance and cloud)

quotes.quote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.

stages.text: God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

payload.title: The genealogy from Adam to Jared
Destruction of the cities of the plain

payload.name: Lot's wife
payload.note: Wife of Lot who looks back at Sodom and becomes a pillar of salt.

stages.label: Lot's wife
stages.text: Lot's wife: a woman of middle age, sturdy and weathered from desert life; olive-brown skin; dark hair bound under a plain linen head-cloth; lined, careful face. Her signature outfit is a long undyed wool wrap over a simple linen tunic in earthy ochre and dun, with leather sandals. She carries no props.

aliases: Abraham the father of many nations
payload.name: Abram
payload.note: Son of Terah from Ur, called to Canaan and renamed Abraham; the same patriarch as Galatians' Abraham, so both entries form one cluster.

stages.label: Abram / Abraham

quotes.quote: Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.
Abraham was one hundred years old when his son, Isaac, was born to him.
Abraham gave up his spirit, and died at a good old age, an old man, and full of years
Lot went with him.

stages.text: Abram, later Abraham: an elderly man of seventy-five to one hundred years and beyond; lean, weathered build from years of travel; dark skin tanned by desert sun; short greying beard and hair; deep-set, steady eyes and lined face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed wool wrap over a earth-brown linen tunic, leather sandals. Signature prop: a long wooden herder's staff.

aliases: the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah
payload.name: Sodom
payload.note: The wicked city of the plain destroyed by fire and sulfur in Genesis, appearing as the cities of the plain and in 2 Peter as Sodom and Gomorrah together; both entries refer to this one place.

stages.label: Sodom

quotes.quote: all the plain of the Jordan, that it was well-watered everywhere
Lot sat in the gate of Sodom.
the valley of Siddim was full of tar pits

stages.text: Sodom: a walled city of sun-dried mud-brick on the well-watered plain of the Jordan, its gate the centre of civic life; flat-roofed houses stacked close, date palms and irrigated gardens beyond the walls, and low hills to the east; the Valley of Siddim nearby, its ground dark with tar pits.

payload.name: Gomorrah
payload.note: Plain city destroyed with Sodom.

stages.label: Gomorrah

quotes.quote: it was well-watered everywhere, before Yahweh destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, like the garden of Yahweh
the valley of Siddim was full of tar pits

stages.text: Gomorrah: a walled mud-brick town on the well-watered plain of the Jordan, flat green pasture and irrigated fields around it, date palms and tamarisk along the ditches, tar pits in the low valley of Siddim to the east, distant hills rising beyond the plain.

payload.title: The sea parts and Israel crosses on dry ground

payload.name: Moses
payload.note: Israel's lawgiver and leader who led the people out of Egypt, received the law at Sinai and is named across the Old and New Testament divisions as the same individual, distinguished only by the sections in which he appears or is mentioned.

stages.label: Moses, elder

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

stages.text: Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.

stages.label: Moses, infant

quotes.quote: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

stages.text: Moses: a newborn infant; soft smooth skin; a small round face; a little dark hair; wrapped in plain linen cloth and laid in a woven reed basket sealed with bitumen and pitch; no beard, no staff, no adult clothing.

stages.label: Moses, adult

quotes.quote: But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

stages.text: Moses: a man of about forty; lean, strong, well-proportioned build; brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard; alert, sober face; a knee-length undyed linen tunic with a dark woven wool cloak of brown and grey pinned at the shoulder; he carries a plain wooden shepherd's staff.

aliases: those who came out of Egypt
payload.name: The Israelite people (the children of Israel)
payload.note: The collective Israelite nation across Exodus through Malachi and Hebrews, one body whose different portrayals (marching nation, assembly, covenant people, judged northern kingdom, returned community, wilderness generation) are all the same people; distinguish only from the returned community of Nehemiah in the note by the Judah/Jerusalem setting, but these are the same people.

stages.label: The Israelite people

quotes.quote: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt
You shall tell the children of Israel this
So they shall put my name on the children of Israel; and I will bless them.

stages.text: The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.

payload.name: the Egyptians
payload.note: The Egyptian people, officers and magicians in Exodus who oppress Israel and suffer the plagues; distinguished from the Egyptian magicians of Genesis and from the Chaldeans of Babylon.

stages.label: the Egyptians

quotes.quote: The Egyptians ruthlessly made the children of Israel serve,
They also, the magicians of Egypt, did the same thing with their enchantments.

stages.text: the Egyptians: adults of middle age, broad-shouldered and strong from labour and rank, with warm brown skin and close-cropped black hair, clean-shaven men with short wigs or bare heads, dignified and grave of face. Signature outfit: a pleated white linen kilt or wrap-tunic with a linen cloak in ochre and blue. Signature props: none carried alone; officers may bear a staff of office.

payload.name: Red Sea
payload.note: The sea in Exodus that parts for Israel and closes over Pharaoh's army; distinct from the other seas by its setting in the exodus narrative.

stages.label: Red Sea

quotes.quote: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and Yahweh caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all night
the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.
You shall encamp opposite it by the sea.

stages.text: Red Sea: a wide, deep arm of open water between desert shores, its surface dark blue-green under wind. Sand dunes and low reddish cliffs line the coast; scattered tamarisk and palms grow at the water's edge. Bare rock outcrops and shallow wadis run down to the shore, and a distant fortified town sits on the northern ridge.

payload.title: Clean and unclean land animals

payload.name: Aaron, brother of Moses
payload.note: Moses' older brother and first high priest, in Exodus and in Numbers (census, offerings, death on Mount Hor); the same man across both divisions.

stages.label: Aaron, the first high priest

quotes.quote: Amram took Jochebed his father’s sister to himself as wife; and she bore him Aaron and Moses.
Of the blue, purple, and scarlet, they made finely worked garments for ministering in the holy place, and made the holy garments for Aaron
Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.

stages.text: Aaron: man in his eighties, older brother of Moses; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and close-cropped hair; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a blue robe, a woven ephod of blue, purple and scarlet, a breastplate, and a linen headband. Props: none carried alone; the rod of the Exodus is sometimes held.

aliases: the tent of meeting outside the camp
payload.name: the camp of Israel
payload.note: The Israelite encampment in the wilderness, with the tent of meeting set outside it in Exodus 33; the same encampment that Leviticus calls the camp.

stages.label: the camp of Israel

quotes.quote: the pillar of cloud moved from before them, and stood behind them.
quail came up and covered the camp; and in the morning the dew lay around the camp.
Moses used to take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, far away from the camp
outside of the camp to a clean place where the ashes are poured out

stages.text: the camp of Israel: a wide wilderness encampment of dun-coloured tents of woven goat-hair cloth in ordered rows, with a central sanctuary tent and a gate; bare stony desert plain, scattered acacia and tamarisk, distant dark mountain slopes; a pillar of cloud above the camp by day and fire by night; ash-pits and a clean place beyond its edges.

payload.title: The Levite's concubine at Gibeah

aliases: the husband of the murdered woman
the man from the hill country of Ephraim
payload.name: The Levite husband of the concubine
payload.note: Levite from the hill country of Ephraim whose concubine is abused and killed at Gibeah; he cuts her body into twelve pieces. Not the young Levite of Bethlehem who serves Micah.

stages.label: The Levite husband of the concubine

quotes.quote: The Levite, the husband of the woman who was murdered, answered

stages.text: The Levite husband of the concubine: a man in his thirties, lean and weathered by travel, with olive skin, short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard shot with grey at the chin. Calm, grave features and steady dark eyes. He wears a plain woven tunic of undyed wool in ochre-brown beneath a long cloak of dusty grey-blue wool. He carries a traveller's staff of dark wood and a leather bag at his hip.

payload.name: The Levite's concubine
payload.note: Concubine of the Levite from Bethlehem Judah, raped and killed at Gibeah in Judges; distinct from Manoah's wife.

stages.label: The Levite's concubine

quotes.quote: She brought him into her father’s house; and when the father of the young lady saw him, he rejoiced to meet him.
the woman his concubine had fallen down at the door of the house, with her hands on the threshold.

stages.text: The Levite's concubine: a young woman in her late teens, slender, of modest height, olive-brown skin, dark hair bound back and covered with a linen veil. Plain woven tunic of undyed wool with a dull red border and a long cloak of rust-brown wool. Simple features, dignified and quiet, with a gentle face. No jewellery beyond a bronze ring.

payload.name: Men of Gibeah
payload.note: The wicked fellows of Gibeah, Benjamites who abuse the Levite's concubine to death; distinct from the Philistines and the tribe of Ephraim.

stages.label: Men of Gibeah

quotes.quote: certain wicked fellows, surrounded the house, beating at the door
They surrounded the Benjamites, chased them, and trod them down

stages.text: Men of Gibeah: adult men of mixed middle age, lean and sun-weathered from village and field life; medium to strong build; warm olive-brown skin; short dark hair and close-cropped beards; hard, set faces with heavy brows. Signature outfit: a woven undyed wool tunic with a rust-brown cloak thrown over the shoulders. Signature prop: a plain wooden cudgel carried at the belt.

payload.name: Bethlehem Judah
payload.note: The one town of Bethlehem in Judah, home of the Levite, Elimelech's family, Jesse and David; the same place across Judges, Ruth and 1 Samuel.

stages.label: Bethlehem Judah

quotes.quote: There was a young man out of Bethlehem Judah, of the family of Judah, who was a Levite; and he lived there.
All the people who were in the gate, and the elders, said
They came to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest.
David went back and forth from Saul to feed his father’s sheep at Bethlehem.

stages.text: Bethlehem Judah: a walled hill town on a limestone ridge in the hill country of Judah, flat-roofed stone and mud-brick houses climbing terraced slopes, a city gate of heavy timber and stone where elders sit, olive groves and vineyards on the terraces, barley fields in the valley below, and a well outside the walls.

payload.name: Gibeah of Benjamin (Judges)
payload.note: The Benjamite city where the Levite's concubine is abused and killed and that is the scene of the war against Benjamin in Judges; distinguish from Saul's Gibeah in 1 Samuel by the Judges events of the concubine and the war.

stages.label: Gibeah of Benjamin

quotes.quote: the sun went down on them near Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin
He went in, and sat down in the street of the city
The children of Israel rose up in the morning and encamped against Gibeah.

stages.text: Gibeah of Benjamin: a fortified hill town of the Benjamite highlands, set on a rocky ridge with terraced slopes. Low houses of mud brick and stone stand close together along a narrow street, flat roofs, and a city wall with a gate. Olive trees, vines and scrub grow on the slopes, with open fields and highways running out of the town.

payload.name: Jebus (Jebusite city before its capture)
payload.note: The earlier name of the same city while held by the Jebusites, before David took it; distinguished by the Jebusite occupation context in the judges entries.

stages.label: Jebus, Jebusite city on the hill

quotes.quote: The children of Judah fought against Jerusalem, took it, struck it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire.
the Jebusites dwell with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.
he rose up and went near Jebus (also called Jerusalem).

stages.text: Jebus: a fortified hill town on a rocky ridge of limestone, with high stone walls of rough-hewn blocks and a strong citadel on the summit; flat-roofed houses of mud brick and stone terraced down the slopes; olive trees and terraced vineyards in the valleys below, a spring-fed water channel at the foot of the hill; a gate tower of weathered stone with dark timber doors.

payload.title: Birth of Obed and the genealogy

payload.name: Ruth
payload.note: Moabite widow of Mahlon who goes with Naomi to Bethlehem, gleans in Boaz's field, becomes Boaz's wife and mother of Obed.

stages.label: Ruth

quotes.quote: The name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the other was Ruth.
It is the Moabite lady who came back with Naomi out of the country of Moab.

stages.text: Ruth: a young woman in her twenties; slender, sturdy build from field labour; warm olive-brown skin; dark hair worn covered with a linen head-veil in the fields and bound back at home; calm, steady face with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a rust-red wool cloak over the shoulders, belted with a cord. Carries a simple woven gleaner's basket on one arm.

payload.name: Boaz
payload.note: Wealthy kinsman of Elimelech in Bethlehem who shows kindness to Ruth, redeems the land and marries her; the one who acts as redeemer at the city gate.

stages.label: Boaz

quotes.quote: a mighty man of wealth, of the family of Elimelech, and his name was Boaz.
Boaz went up to the gate and sat down there.

stages.text: Boaz: a mature man in his middle years, broad-shouldered and sturdy, of a prosperous landholder. Olive-brown skin weathered by the fields. Dark hair and a short, neatly trimmed beard with some grey at the temples. Calm, dignified face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long undertunic of undyed linen under a cloak of deep blue wool with a woven band at the hem. Carries a shepherd's staff of olive wood.

payload.name: Naomi
payload.note: Wife of Elimelech, mother of Mahlon and Chilion, mother-in-law of Ruth and Orpah; returns from Moab to Bethlehem and calls herself Mara; cares for Ruth's son.

stages.label: Naomi

quotes.quote: The name of the man was Elimelech, and the name of his wife Naomi.
Call me Mara, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.
I went out full, and Yahweh has brought me home again empty.
Naomi took the child, laid him in her bosom, and became nurse to him.

stages.text: Naomi: woman of middle years, mature and weathered by grief; lean, upright build; olive skin with sun-darkened forearms; dark hair covered by a plain linen veil, with grey threads showing at the temples; lined face, dignified and steady; wears an undyed brown woollen tunic with a long dull-ochre cloak over it, belted at the waist; carries a small water skin or walking staff alone.

payload.name: Women of Bethlehem
payload.note: The neighborhood women of Bethlehem who praise Naomi and name Obed in Ruth; distinct from the women weeping for Tammuz at the north gate in Ezekiel 8.

stages.label: Women of Bethlehem

quotes.quote: They took for themselves wives of the women of Moab.
The women said to Naomi, “Blessed be Yahweh, who has not left you today without a near kinsman.
The women, her neighbors, gave him a name, saying, “A son is born to Naomi”.

stages.text: Women of Bethlehem: adult village women, mature to middle age; sturdy, unhurried build; warm olive-brown skin; dark hair covered by a plain linen headcloth; weathered, kind faces with lines of work and years; signature outfit a long undyed linen tunic under a dun-brown woven cloak; no props carried alone.

payload.name: Naomi's house in Bethlehem
payload.note: Ruth and Naomi's home in Bethlehem where the child is cared for; distinct from Boaz's fields and the threshing floor.

stages.label: Naomi's house in Bethlehem

quotes.quote: each of you in the house of her husband
except that she rested a little in the house
the woman who has come into your house

stages.text: Naomi's house in Bethlehem: a modest village dwelling of mud-brick walls and a flat roof of packed earth and beams, with a low doorway and a courtyard of beaten earth. Stone terraces and olive trees stand on the hillside, with grain fields in the valley below and the walls of Bethlehem nearby.

payload.title: David kills Goliath

aliases: the anointed of the God of Jacob
payload.name: David son of Jesse (king of Israel)
payload.note: The single David of the Hebrew books and the New Testament references: son of Jesse, shepherd, harpist, anointed king, father of Solomon; all entries describe this one king and the hint's second David is not needed.

stages.label: David as king

quotes.quote: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.

stages.text: David: a man of about thirty to fifty, athletic and broad-shouldered, of medium height; ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes, short dark beard trimmed close; dark hair cut to the shoulder. Signature outfit: a long blue royal robe with a sash of crimson and gold, over an undertunic of white linen. Carries a bronze-bossed sword in a leather scabbard and a harp.

stages.label: David as youth

quotes.quote: He sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with a handsome face and good appearance. Yahweh said, “Arise! Anoint him, for this is he.”

stages.text: David: a beardless youth and young adult before kingship; slender, wiry build, ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes and short dark curly hair. Plain undyed brown wool tunic, leather belt and sandals; shepherd's pouch and sling when called for. No crown or royal robes.

stages.label: David as elder

quotes.quote: Now King David was old and advanced in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he couldn’t keep warm.

stages.text: David: an old man of about seventy, lean and bent with age, his frame still dignified; ruddy complexion faded to a weathered warmth, dark eyes deep-set and gentle, white hair and a white beard cut short. Signature outfit: a plain long wool robe of undyed cream with a dark blue cloak over the shoulders for warmth. Carries a staff of almond wood.

payload.name: Goliath
payload.note: Giant Philistine champion of Gath who challenges Israel and is killed by David.

stages.label: Goliath of Gath

quotes.quote: A champion out of the camp of the Philistines named Goliath of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span went out.
the champion, the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name, came up out of the ranks of the Philistines
Behold, the sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you killed in the valley of Elah

stages.text: Goliath: man of enormous height, over nine feet tall, broad-shouldered and heavily muscled, around forty years old. Olive-brown skin, close-cropped dark hair and a full dark beard, strong heavy brow, grave and hard features. Wears bronze scale armour over a linen tunic, bronze greaves, and a bronze helmet, colours of bronze, dark leather and undyed linen. Carries a great spear with a heavy iron head and a sword at his side.

payload.name: Saul
payload.note: First king of Israel, son of Kish.

stages.label: Saul, first king of Israel

quotes.quote: Am I not a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel?
Saul disguised himself and put on other clothing
they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.

stages.text: Saul: a man in his forties, tall and broad-shouldered with a strong, weathered face, dark hair cut to the neck and a short, close beard. Skin olive-brown from sun. Dignified, brooding eyes. Signature outfit: a long undertunic of deep blue wool under a dark red royal cloak with a gold-bordered hem, a bronze-scaled leather belt and a plain sandal. Carries a royal spear of dark ash wood with a bronze head.

payload.name: Abner son of Ner
payload.note: Captain of Saul's army and Saul's uncle in Samuel, who later makes Ishbosheth king and is killed by Joab at Hebron in Samuel 2.

stages.label: Abner son of Ner

quotes.quote: Abner the son of Ner, Saul’s uncle.
Am I a dog’s head that belongs to Judah?

stages.text: Abner son of Ner: a man of middle to later years, broad-shouldered and sturdy, with a dignified, weathered face. Skin olive-brown from the sun. Hair dark, graying at the temples, worn to the shoulder; a short, close-cut grey-streaked beard. Wears a long undertunic and a cloak of deep blue over bronze scale armour, with a leather sword belt. Carries a long spear and a bronze-hilted sword.

payload.name: Philistines
payload.note: The oppressors of Israel and lords of the Philistines in Samson's story; a foreign people, not an Israelite tribe.

stages.label: Philistines (typical warrior of the lords' armies)

quotes.quote: the five lords of the Philistines
thirty thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen

stages.text: Philistines: adult men of the coastal cities, age twenty to forty; medium-to-broad build, sun-browned skin; close-cropped dark hair and a short beard; calm, hard-set features, not caricatured. Typical dress: a knee-length woven tunic of undyed wool with a bordered hem in blue or red, a leather belt and a short cloak of dark wool. Signature props: a bronze helmet with a crest and a round shield, carried by the army; no props carried by the figure alone.

payload.name: Valley of Elah
payload.note: Valley in 1 Samuel between the armies where David fights and kills Goliath.

stages.label: Valley of Elah

quotes.quote: encamped in the valley of Elah, and set the battle in array against the Philistines

stages.text: Valley of Elah: a broad, shallow valley of the Judean lowlands between rounded hills of terraced limestone, with a dry watercourse winding through its floor. Scattered terebinth and oak trees and low scrub grow along the slopes, and sun-baked earth shows pale between rocks. Rough stone walls and simple dwellings of field stone mark the hill ridges.

payload.name: Gath (Philistine city)
payload.note: The Philistine city where the ark was taken, Goliath's home, and David's refuge; distinct from the Judahite villages named in Micah.

stages.label: Gath, Philistine city

quotes.quote: They carried the ark of the God of Israel there.
A champion out of the camp of the Philistines named Goliath of Gath
went to Achish the king of Gath.
David lived with Achish at Gath

stages.text: Gath: a fortified Philistine city on a low hill of the Shephelah, reached by a dusty road from the lowland fields. Thick mudbrick and stone city walls crowned with timber towers, a broad gate of heavy timber and bronze fittings, and tall stone-and-mudbrick houses with flat roofs clustered inside. Olive groves, terraced vineyards and grain fields spread beyond the walls; sycamore and terebinth stand along the road. Cult stands and a temple precinct rise above the houses.

payload.title: Youths mock Elisha at Bethel

payload.name: Elisha son of Shaphat
payload.note: Prophet, Elijah's successor, who first appears as a farmer plowing with twelve yoke of oxen in 1 Kings and is later named in 2 Kings and Luke; the same prophet in all three entries.

stages.label: Elisha son of Shaphat

quotes.quote: found Elisha the son of Shaphat, who was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen before him
Elijah went over to him and put his mantle on him.
He took Elijah’s mantle that fell from him
He went up from there to Bethel. As he was going up by the way, some youths came out of the city and mocked him, and said to him, “Go up, you baldy! Go up, you baldy!”

stages.text: Elisha son of Shaphat: a man in his middle years, broad-shouldered and sun-browned from working the fields, lean and steady in build. Dark skin, a bald head, and a close-cut beard with some grey at the chin. Calm, weathered face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a cloak of rough brown wool. Signature prop: Elijah's mantle, a dark sheepskin cloak he wears over his shoulders.

payload.name: Bethel (prophets' community and calf shrine in Kings)
payload.note: Town in 2 Kings with a prophets' community and golden-calf shrine, where Elisha is mocked by youths and Josiah acts against the shrine; the same northern shrine tradition as in 1 Kings.

stages.label: Bethel, hill town with calf shrine

quotes.quote: So they went down to Bethel.
some youths came out of the city
the golden calves that were in Bethel and that were in Dan
the altar that was at Bethel and the high place

stages.text: Bethel: a walled hill town on a rocky ridge of central Judah-Israel highland, terraced olive groves and terebinths on the slopes, low flat-roofed stone and mud-brick houses, a city gate of heavy timber and stone, and a raised high place with an altar of dressed stone and an Asherah pole beside it, with the golden-calf shrine as its central landmark.

payload.name: Mount Carmel
payload.note: The Carmel of Elijah's contest with the prophets of Baal and of his and Elisha's later presence in Kings.

stages.label: Mount Carmel

quotes.quote: Now therefore send, and gather to me all Israel to Mount Carmel
Elijah went up to the top of Carmel

stages.text: Mount Carmel: a long, rounded limestone ridge rising above the Mediterranean coast, its slopes covered with low scrub, oak, terebinth and wild flowers, bare rock outcrops at the crest, a broad flat summit suitable for an altar, and an old stone-built altar site among the rocks.

payload.name: Samaria (city)
payload.note: The northern kingdom's capital city, the hill of Samaria founded by Omri, besieged and fallen as described in Kings, Chronicles, Amos and Micah; foreign peoples are settled in the city in Ezra 4:10, and Philip preaches in the city in Acts. Distinct from the wider region and from Sychar.

stages.label: Samaria, hill capital

quotes.quote: He bought the hill Samaria of Shemer for two talents of silver; and he built on the hill
He raised up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal, which he had built in Samaria.
in an open place at the entrance of the gate of Samaria
They washed the chariot by the pool of Samaria
the city of Samaria, and in the rest of the country beyond the River

stages.text: Samaria: a broad, steep hill rising alone out of the central hill country, its slopes terraced with olive and vine. Walls of dressed limestone ring the crown, with a gate opening onto an open place by the entrance. Within stand a royal palace of cut stone and cedar beams, a house of Baal with an altar, and a pool at the foot of the hill.

payload.title: Yahweh speaks from the whirlwind

payload.name: Job
payload.note: Blameless, wealthy man of Uz who loses his family and health and debates with his friends and with Yahweh.

stages.label: Job

quotes.quote: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, and one who feared God, and turned away from evil.
Then Job arose, and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down on the ground, and worshiped.
So Satan went out from the presence of Yahweh, and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to his head.

stages.text: Job: man of middle to later years, perhaps fifty to sixty, of sturdy but weathered build; dark brown skin; short, graying hair with a close-trimmed beard shaved at the head in grief; dignified, lined face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a deep indigo wool cloak over it. Carries a shepherd's staff of olive wood. Sores on skin in later sections.

payload.name: The whirlwind
payload.note: Place from which Yahweh speaks to Job (38:1, 40:6).

stages.label: The whirlwind

quotes.quote: Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind,
Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind:

stages.text: The whirlwind: a great column of storm wind rising from a dark wilderness sky, funnelling dust, torn cloud and scattered grit in dense swirling bands. Heavy grey-brown cloud churns above, its edges lit faintly from behind. Low scrub and bare desert ground are flattened and whipped by the gale.

payload.name: The ash heap
payload.note: Place outside the city where Job sits, scraping his sores with a potsherd (2:8).

stages.label: The ash heap

quotes.quote: He took for himself a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.
houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust

stages.text: The ash heap: a broad low mound of grey and white ash, dust and broken clay outside the city walls, sloping gently to bare dry ground. Scattered potsherds, cracked jars and cinders lie in drifts; sparse scrub and thorn bushes grow at its edges. Distant city walls, gates and roofs of sun-baked brick rise on the horizon.

payload.title: Isaiah's vision of Yahweh in the temple

payload.name: Isaiah son of Amoz
payload.note: Prophet who advises Hezekiah; the same prophet across Isaiah, 2 Kings and 2 Chronicles.

stages.label: Isaiah son of Amoz

quotes.quote: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Go, and loosen the sackcloth from off your waist, and take your sandals from off your feet.

stages.text: Isaiah son of Amoz: a man in his fifties, lean and sinewy, with a weathered brown skin of the Judean hill country. Dark hair graying at the temples, worn to the shoulders, and a short, full grey beard. Deep-set, steady eyes and a long, lined face marked by years of hard counsel. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist and a rough brown wool cloak in earth tones. Carries a simple wooden staff, the sign of a traveling prophet.

payload.name: Seraphim
payload.note: Six-winged beings around the throne in Isaiah 6 who call out and touch Isaiah's lips with a coal; a class of heavenly beings, not a single individual.

stages.label: Seraphim

quotes.quote: Each one had six wings. With two he covered his face. With two he covered his feet. With two he flew.
one of the seraphim flew to me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar.

stages.text: Seraphim: a heavenly being of tall, luminous human-like form, ageless, with burnished bronze-gold skin. Six wings: two cover the face, two cover the feet, two lift in flight, feathered in white and gold. Face hidden behind the wings. Robed in a long linen tunic of pale white. Carries a glowing live coal held in long iron tongs, the coal burning orange-red.

aliases: the house which is called by my name
the tent of the daughter of Zion
the house of Yahweh of Armies
payload.name: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem (the temple)
payload.note: The one Jerusalem temple (Yahweh's house, the sanctuary on Mount Moriah) across all references, from Solomon's building through repair, destruction and rebuilding; construction and ruin are later appearance stages, not separate places.

stages.label: Solomon's temple on Mount Moriah

quotes.quote: The house, when it was under construction, was built of stone prepared at the quarry
Within the inner sanctuary was twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in width, and twenty cubits in its height.
He overlaid the floor of the house with gold, inside and outside.
Also he made before the house two pillars thirty-five cubits high
He set the sea on the right side of the house eastward and toward the south.

stages.text: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem: a stone temple of finished ashlar on Mount Moriah, roofed with cedar beams, its inner sanctuary panelled in cedar and overlaid with pure gold. Carved cherubim, palm and open flowers cover the doors and walls. Before the house stand two great bronze pillars and a huge bronze molten sea on twelve oxen. Courts of stone surround it, with olive and cypress trees, and the walled city of Jerusalem rises beyond.

payload.title: Vision of the valley of dry bones

payload.name: Ezekiel son of Buzi
payload.note: Exiled priest and prophet at the river Chebar.

stages.label: Ezekiel son of Buzi

quotes.quote: Yahweh’s word came to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar

stages.text: Ezekiel son of Buzi: a man of about thirty, lean and steady, with dark hair and a short trimmed beard, bronze-brown skin from desert sun, and a calm, watchful face. He wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic with a long cloak of rough brown wool over it. He carries a wooden writing tablet and stylus.

payload.name: Valley of dry bones
payload.note: Valley full of bones that Ezekiel sees revived in vision.

stages.label: Valley of dry bones
stages.text: Valley of dry bones: a wide, low valley floor of pale, sun-bleached earth and grey-brown stony ground, with scattered dry scrub and no living green. Ridges of bare rock rise on either side under a broad, open sky. Across the valley floor lie countless bleached human bones, skulls, ribs and long limbs, dry and separate, with no buildings, gates or walls in sight.

payload.title: Daniel delivered from the lions

payload.name: Darius the Mede
payload.note: Mede who takes the kingdom after Belshazzar, sets Daniel over his realm and casts him into the lions' den; a different ruler from the Persian king of Ezra.

stages.label: Darius the Mede

quotes.quote: Darius the Mede received the kingdom, being about sixty-two years old.

stages.text: Darius the Mede: early sixties; broad, settled build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and hair under a tall royal cap; lined, steady face with heavy brows. Signature outfit: a long purple court robe over a cream tunic, with a gold-embroidered collar and a deep blue sash. Signature prop: a signet ring of gold on his right hand.

payload.name: Daniel (prophet of Babylon)
payload.note: The Jewish youth taken captive to Babylon, renamed Belteshazzar, who interprets dreams and receives visions; the main entry with many sections in Daniel, distinguished from the prophet named only in Matthew's citation.

stages.label: Daniel (Belteshazzar), prophet of Babylon

quotes.quote: Now among these of the children of Judah were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
to Daniel he gave the name Belteshazzar
he went into his house (now his windows were open in his room toward Jerusalem)

stages.text: Daniel: a lean, dignified Judean man, grave and greying; olive-brown skin; close-cropped greying hair and a short trimmed grey beard; deep-set, steady eyes and a calm, thoughtful face. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic under a plain indigo wool cloak with a blue fringed hem. Props: a small leather scroll case slung at the hip.

payload.name: the den of lions
payload.note: Pit into which Daniel is cast and from which he is delivered.

stages.label: The den of lions

quotes.quote: they brought Daniel and cast him into the den of lions
went in haste to the den of lions

stages.text: The den of lions: a deep circular stone pit cut into bare earth beside a royal enclosure, its walls of dressed grey limestone rising high above a sandy floor. A heavy wooden lid and an iron-banded gate sit at the rim, reached by a worn stone stair. Dry scrub and a few palms grow at the edge; no plants inside the pit.

payload.title: The Ancient of Days and the son of man

payload.name: The Ancient of Days
payload.note: The divine figure on a fiery throne in Daniel's vision of the beasts; a distinct visionary figure, seen only in Daniel's dream-vision.

stages.label: The Ancient of Days

quotes.quote: His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool.
His throne was fiery flames, and its wheels burning fire.
A fiery stream issued and came out from before him.

stages.text: The Ancient of Days: brilliant white radiance; bright orange fire; soft white cloud; brilliant white light.

aliases: one like a son of man
payload.name: One like a son of man
payload.note: The figure coming with the clouds of heaven to receive dominion in Daniel's vision; not the Gospel Jesus, but a distinct heavenly figure in Daniel.

stages.label: One like a son of man

quotes.quote: there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the Ancient of Days

stages.text: One like a son of man: a man in his prime, early thirties, of athletic but dignified build; skin warm olive-brown; short dark hair and a close-cut beard; calm, steady features with a grave, luminous gaze. He wears a long white linen tunic with a deep blue-purple cloak falling from the shoulders, edged with gold thread. He carries no props.

payload.name: Babylon
payload.note: The city and empire of exile and captivity across the prophets, histories and psalms, also called Babylonia, Shinar and the land of the Chaldeans; the same place in every division.

stages.label: Babylon

quotes.quote: The wide walls of Babylon will be utterly overthrown. Her high gates will be burned with fire.
I will execute judgment on Bel in Babylon, and I will bring out of his mouth that which he has swallowed up.
He brought the vessels into the treasure house of his god.
I will record Rahab and Babylon among those who acknowledge me.

stages.text: Babylon: a vast walled city of baked brick on a flat plain watered by broad canals and rivers, its wide walls rising high and its great gates of bronze-banded cedar. Date palms and reed beds line the riverbanks, and ziggurat towers and palace roofs of brick rise above the flat skyline, with the temple of Bel among them.

payload.name: Ministering assembly in Daniel's vision
payload.note: The unidentified assembly ministering before the Ancient of Days in Daniel 7:10; distinct from earthly Babylonian royal attendants. A group whose canon describes a typical member.

stages.label: Ministering assembly

quotes.quote: A fiery stream issued and came out from before him. Thousands of thousands ministered to him. Ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. The judgment was set. The books were opened.

stages.text: Ministering assembly in Daniel's vision: a typical member is an adult of medium height and slim build, with warm brown skin, dark curly hair and a short dark beard, wearing an undyed linen robe, a narrow woven belt and plain sandals.

payload.title: Genealogy of Jesus
Peter walks on water

aliases: the apostle and high priest of our confession
the great shepherd of the sheep
the author and perfecter of faith
the mediator of a new covenant
the Lion of the tribe of Judah
the rider called Faithful and True
KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS
payload.name: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord
payload.note: The one Jesus: the teacher from Nazareth of the Gospels and Acts, and the risen, exalted Christ and Lord of the epistles and Revelation; the same individual across all divisions, with death, resurrection and changed portrayal not creating new individuals.

stages.label: Adult Jesus

quotes.quote: Jesus himself, when he began to teach, was about thirty years old, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli,

stages.text: Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.

stages.label: Infant Jesus

quotes.quote: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.

stages.text: Jesus: newborn to about two years old; olive-brown skin, a little dark hair and dark eyes; a small infant or toddler's build, no beard. Plain undyed swaddling linen for the newborn; a small plain linen tunic as a toddler. No adult clothing or props.

stages.label: Boy Jesus

quotes.quote: When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast;

stages.text: Jesus: boy of about twelve, slim and sturdy; olive-brown skin; dark brown hair cut short at the neck; dark eyes; no beard; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak; no props.

payload.name: Simon Peter
payload.note: The fisherman apostle, first-called disciple and leader of the twelve, who appears in the Gospels, Acts, Galatians and both letters of Peter; all entries here are the same individual, distinguished only by role and portrayal.

stages.label: Simon Peter

quotes.quote: Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew, his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.
You are Simon the son of Jonah. You shall be called Cephas

stages.text: Simon Peter: a sturdy man in his thirties, broad-shouldered from hauling nets, weathered brown skin from sun on the Sea of Galilee, short dark curly hair and a full beard flecked with grey. Plain undyed tunic of natural linen under a rough brown wool cloak. Signature props: a coiled fishing net over one shoulder and a wooden fishing staff.

payload.name: The Twelve Disciples (collective)
payload.note: The twelve apostles/disciples as one collective body acting together across the Gospels and Acts; distinct from the individual disciples named within them.

stages.label: The Twelve Disciples (collective)

quotes.quote: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these. The first, Simon, who is called Peter; Andrew, his brother; James the son of Zebedee
One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to him,

stages.text: The Twelve Disciples: men of about twenty to forty years; sun-browned, lean and sturdy from fishing and walking; olive to weathered brown skin; short or shoulder-length dark hair and close-trimmed beards; plain, earnest faces. Signature outfit: a undyed linen tunic and a rough brown wool cloak with fringed hem. Signature props: a fishing net coiled over one shoulder for Peter and Andrew; a walking staff for travelers.

payload.name: Sea of Galilee
payload.note: The lake of Galilee (also called Gennesaret or Tiberias) where Jesus calls fishermen, calms the storm, and teaches by the shore; the common lake identity across the Gospels.

stages.label: Sea of Galilee

quotes.quote: Walking by the sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers
he entered into a boat in the sea and sat down. All the multitude were on the land by the sea.
He saw two boats standing by the lake, but the fishermen had gone out of them and were washing their nets.

stages.text: Sea of Galilee: a large freshwater lake set in hilly terrain of basalt and limestone, its shores sloping to pebbled and sandy beaches. Low stone-built fishing villages and wooden fishing boats line the water, with nets drying on the shore. Reeds, oleanders and palms grow along the banks, and fig and olive trees climb the hills above.

payload.name: the boat (Matthew's sea boat)
payload.note: The fishing boat in Matthew used for crossings and during the storm, and the setting for the parables taught from the boat; distinguished from John's lake shore by being the boat of the storm and parable accounts.

stages.label: the boat (Matthew's sea boat)

quotes.quote: in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets
the boat was now in the middle of the sea, distressed by the waves

stages.text: the boat (Matthew's sea boat): a small open fishing boat of dark weathered timber, planked and caulked with pitch, with a low curved hull, one mast and a brown-tan sail patched with mended net; oars lie along the thwarts; coiled nets and a ropes are stowed at the bow; sea-grey lake water and reed-fringed shore.

payload.title: Miraculous catch and breakfast on the shore

payload.name: Thomas the apostle
payload.note: One of the twelve apostles, called Didymus or the Twin; the same disciple in every division, including the John account where he doubts until he sees Jesus.

stages.label: Thomas the apostle

quotes.quote: Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus
Thomas therefore, who is called Didymus

stages.text: Thomas the apostle: a man in his thirties, lean and sturdy from fishing and travel. Olive-brown skin, weathered by sun. Short dark curly hair and a close-cut beard flecked with grey at the chin. Deep-set, earnest eyes and a furrowed brow suggesting thought and grief. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic in ochre with a dark brown woollen cloak. Carries a worn leather travelling satchel across one shoulder.

payload.name: Bartholomew
payload.note: One of the twelve apostles, also called Nathanael in John; the same apostle appears in all four entries, so the four keys form a single cluster.

stages.label: Bartholomew / Nathanael

quotes.quote: Behold, an Israelite indeed, in whom is no deceit!
Can any good thing come out of Nazareth?

stages.text: Bartholomew (Nathanael): a man in his thirties, lean and sun-weathered, with olive-brown skin, short dark hair and a close-cut beard flecked with grey. Calm, direct eyes and a plain, open face. Signature outfit: a sleeveless undertunic of undyed linen under a faded indigo-blue wool cloak. Carries no props apart from a leather fishing satchel at the belt.

payload.name: James and John, sons of Zebedee
payload.note: Two brothers, disciples of Jesus, who ask for seats at his right and left and later fish with Peter at the lake; both entries describe this same pair, so they are one cluster.

stages.label: James and John, sons of Zebedee

quotes.quote: James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came near to him
the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples were together

stages.text: James and John, sons of Zebedee: young men in their twenties, lean and weathered from lake work; brown skin, dark curly hair cut short above the ears, closely trimmed beards; sun-creased faces, steady eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic in earth brown with a rough wool cloak in faded blue-grey. Signature prop: a coiled fishing net slung over one shoulder.

payload.name: The beloved disciple
payload.note: Unnamed disciple in the Gospel of John who leans on Jesus at supper, stands at the cross and runs to the tomb; traditionally identified with the apostle John but not named in these sections.

stages.label: The beloved disciple

quotes.quote: the disciple whom Jesus loved, the one who had also leaned on Jesus’ chest at the supper
The other disciple outran Peter and came to the tomb first.

stages.text: The beloved disciple: a young man of about thirty, lean and quick, with a sun-browned skin of the Galilean fishing shore. Dark brown hair cut just above the ears, a short, close beard, and a calm, steady, attentive face with deep-set eyes. He wears a plain undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown under a dark wool cloak of earth brown. He carries a simple wooden walking staff.

payload.title: Calming the storm
Parable of the prodigal son

payload.name: the younger son
payload.note: Younger son in the parable of the lost son (ch. 15).

stages.label: the younger son

quotes.quote: the younger son gathered all of this together and traveled into a far country

stages.text: the younger son: Young man in his late teens or early twenties, slender and wiry, with a lean build. Olive skin browned by travel and weather. Dark hair cut short and unkempt, with a short, sparse beard. Face young and open, with weary eyes and a tired mouth. Signature outfit: a sun-faded undyed linen tunic with a dust-brown woollen cloak. Signature prop: a small leather purse at his belt.

payload.name: The prodigal's father
payload.note: Unnamed father of the two sons in Luke's parable of the prodigal son, who welcomes his younger son home.

stages.label: The prodigal's father

quotes.quote: Bring out the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.

stages.text: The prodigal's father: man in his late fifties to sixties, of middle height and sturdy, weathered build from years of farm labour; olive skin, lined with sun; close-cropped grey-streaked dark hair and a short greying beard; deep-set, kind eyes and a broad, steady face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown under a dark russet woollen cloak, with a fringed tzitzit at the hem. Signature props: none carried alone; a bronze signet ring on his hand.

payload.name: Galilee
payload.note: The northern region of Galilee where Jesus preaches, teaches and heals; both Matthew and Luke describe the same region, so these entries are one place.

stages.label: Galilee

quotes.quote: Walking by the sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers
teaching in their synagogues, preaching the Good News of the Kingdom
toward the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles

stages.text: Galilee: Northern hill country falling to a freshwater lake, the sea of Galilee, its shore lined with fishing boats and nets drying on stone. Low limestone villages of flat-roofed houses, a white stone synagogue with a shallow portico, terraced olive groves, fig trees and scrubland. Roman roads and a distant Gentile town on the slopes.

payload.title: Lazarus raised from the tomb

payload.name: Martha
payload.note: Woman of Bethany who serves Jesus in her house and is the sister of Mary; not the same as Miriam, the sister of Moses and Aaron.

stages.label: Martha of Bethany

quotes.quote: a certain woman named Martha received him into her house
Martha was distracted with much serving
Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus.

stages.text: Martha of Bethany: a woman in her thirties, of sturdy and capable build, with warm olive skin weathered by sun. Dark brown hair is covered by a plain linen head veil pulled back from a careful face with a firm mouth and tired, attentive eyes. Her signature outfit, worn most often, is an undyed ochre-brown tunic with a rust-red wool cloak over the shoulders, belted with a plain cord. She carries no signature props.

payload.name: Lazarus of Bethany
payload.note: Man of Bethany, brother of Mary and Martha, raised from the tomb after four days (John); distinct from the beggar in Luke's parable.

stages.label: Lazarus of Bethany

quotes.quote: a certain man was sick, Lazarus from Bethany, of the village of Mary and her sister, Martha.
Lazarus was one of those who sat at the table with him.

stages.text: Lazarus of Bethany: man in his thirties; lean, medium build; olive skin weathered by sun; short dark hair and close-trimmed beard, streaked grey at the chin; calm, steady face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: plain undyed linen tunic in ochre-brown, with a dark wool cloak in earth-brown. Carries no props.

payload.name: Crowd in John
payload.note: Large crowds who follow Jesus, are fed at the five thousand and debate his identity in John's gospel.

stages.label: Crowd in John

quotes.quote: So the men sat down, in number about five thousand.
There was much murmuring among the multitudes concerning him.

stages.text: Crowd in John: adults and some older children of Jewish and Gentile communities in Galilee and Judea, ages roughly 15 to 60; lean to sturdy build; olive to tan skin; dark or grey-streaked hair kept short or tied back, beards kept trimmed or unshaven among the men; plain, weathered faces showing the sun and labour. Signature outfit: a undyed linen or wool tunic in ochre, earth brown or faded blue, with a long woollen cloak in dusty ochre, worn over the shoulders. Carries nothing alone.

payload.title: Saul's vision on the road to Damascus

payload.name: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)
payload.note: Pharisee from Tarsus who persecutes the Way, is converted on the road to Damascus, and becomes the apostle Paul; told apart from the king by his Pharisee and Tarsus background and conversion narrative in Acts.

stages.label: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)

quotes.quote: The witnesses placed their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
They led him by the hand and brought him into Damascus.
I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees.
But I was born a Roman.

stages.text: Saul/Paul: man in his thirties to fifties, middle height and spare, wiry build worn by travel and hardship. Olive-brown skin, dark hair cropped short, close-trimmed dark beard with grey beginning at the chin. Lined forehead, deep-set dark eyes, strong nose. Signature outfit: plain undyed wool tunic in ochre-brown under a dark brown travelling cloak with a fringed hem. Signature prop: a worn leather writing satchel and a plain wooden walking staff.

payload.name: the men with Saul
payload.note: Men traveling with Saul to Damascus who hear the voice but see no one.

stages.label: Travelling companion of Saul
stages.text: The men with Saul: adult men, late twenties to forties; sturdy, lean build from road travel; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and close-cropped beard; plain, weathered faces. Signature outfit: a undyed linen tunic with a brown wool travelling cloak in dusty earth tones. Carries a walking staff and a leather satchel.

payload.name: Damascus
payload.note: Capital city of Syria, seat of Ben-hadad and Rezon, and home of Naaman's rivers, judged in Amos and linked with Paul's conversion and escape in Acts and 2 Corinthians; all entries here are the same city.

stages.label: Damascus

quotes.quote: synagogues of Damascus
the rivers of Damascus
guarded the Damascenes’ city
went up against Damascus and took it

stages.text: Damascus: a walled oasis city of pale limestone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs and domes, set against arid hills; date palms, orchards and irrigated gardens watered by the rivers Abanah and Pharpar; a city gate with a wall, and a straight main street lined with walls and shaded arcades.

payload.title: Creation groans and the Spirit's intercession

aliases: my child's father in the faith
the aged prisoner of Christ Jesus
payload.name: Paul the apostle
payload.note: The apostle Paul, author and speaker of all thirteen letters; the same individual across Romans, Corinthians, Galatians, Ephesians, Philippians, Colossians, Thessalonians, Timothy, Titus and Philemon, identified by his apostolic authorship and first-person voice.

stages.label: Paul the apostle

quotes.quote: being such a one as Paul, the aged, but also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. Remember my chains.
I, Paul, write this with my own hand

stages.text: Paul the apostle: man of middle to later years, perhaps fifties to sixties, wiry and weathered from travel and imprisonment; Jewish Mediterranean features, olive-brown skin, short greying-dark beard and close-cropped hair receding at the temples; lined brow, steady dark eyes. Signature outfit: plain undyed wool tunic in ochre-brown under a dark-blue cloak. Signature prop: a rolled parchment scroll and a reed pen case at the belt.

payload.title: Way to Golgotha; the crucifixion

payload.name: Simon of Cyrene
payload.note: Cyrenian man compelled to carry Jesus' cross; the father of Alexander and Rufus in Mark; distinct from every other Simon in the group.

stages.label: Simon of Cyrene

quotes.quote: Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus
coming from the country

stages.text: Simon of Cyrene: a man in his forties, sturdy and broad-shouldered from years of field labour; olive-brown skin weathered by sun; short dark hair and a close-cropped beard streaked with grey; a lined, steady face with deep-set dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist, with a rough brown wool cloak thrown over the shoulders, dusty from the road. No signature props.

payload.name: The Roman soldiers
payload.note: Roman soldiers (and Herodian soldiers in Luke) who mock, crucify and guard Jesus across all three Gospels; they are one body of soldiers seen from different accounts, so all three entries describe the same group.

stages.label: The Roman soldiers

quotes.quote: Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the Praetorium, and gathered the whole garrison together against him.
The soldiers twisted thorns into a crown and put it on his head, and dressed him in a purple garment.
Now the tunic was without seam, woven from the top throughout.

stages.text: The Roman soldiers: adult men, late twenties to forties; sturdy, disciplined build; olive to tan skin of Mediterranean men; short-cropped dark or brown hair, clean-shaven or close-cropped beard; stern, weathered faces. Signature dress: a short tunic of undyed linen under a red-brown woollen military cloak, leather belt and sandals, bronze helmet worn at the cohort. Props: a short sword at the hip and a tall rectangular shield.

payload.name: Golgotha
payload.note: The hill outside Jerusalem called the place of a skull, where Jesus is crucified; the Matthew and John entries describe the same place and join here.

stages.label: Golgotha

quotes.quote: When they came to a place called “Golgotha”, that is to say, “The place of a skull,”
When they came to the place that is called “The Skull”
He went out, bearing his cross, to the place called “The Place of a Skull”

stages.text: Golgotha: a rounded rocky knoll of pale limestone rising just outside the walls of Jerusalem, bare of trees and scrub except for thin dry grass in cracks. Its crown is worn smooth and bony-white, giving the hill its name, the place of a skull. A rough stone-cut quarry face and a few low olive trees stand at its foot, and the walls and towers of the city rise distant behind it.

payload.title: Living creatures and the elders worship

payload.name: John the seer (Revelation)
payload.note: Author and visionary on Patmos who receives and records the revelation; the narrator of Revelation, distinct from other Johns.

stages.label: John the seer

quotes.quote: to his servant, John
I John, your brother and partner with you in the oppression

stages.text: John the seer: man of about sixty, of middle height and spare build, weathered olive skin from exile by the sea, short greying hair and a close grey beard, lined brow and steady dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown under a rough dark brown wool mantle. He carries a worn wooden staff and a small scroll case.

aliases: the creature with a face like a man
payload.name: Four living creatures (Revelation)
payload.note: The creatures around God's throne in Revelation, full of eyes, who worship God and call forth the four horsemen; distinguished from the Ezekiel beings by their role at the throne and the seals.

stages.label: Four living creatures

quotes.quote: each one of them having six wings, are full of eyes around and within
as though it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes

stages.text: Four living creatures: ageless and powerful, each with six wings set close about the body; the wings and bodies are covered with eyes, around and within. One is lion-like with a mane of tawny gold, one calf-like with a sleek red-brown hide, one with a human face of grave dignity and dark skin, one eagle-like with bronze-gold feathers. Robes of deep crimson and white.

payload.name: Twenty-four elders of Revelation
payload.note: Twenty-four elders seated on thrones around God's throne, clothed in white with golden crowns.

stages.label: Twenty-four elders of Revelation

quotes.quote: the twenty-four elders fall down before him who sits on the throne
each one having a harp, and golden bowls full of incense
These who are arrayed in the white robes, who are they

stages.text: Twenty-four elders: mature men of venerable age, grey or white-bearded, of dignified and grounded build; skin warm olive-brown; hair white and worn to the shoulder, full white beard; calm, noble faces. Signature outfit: long white robes with gold sashes and a golden crown on the head. Props, carried alone: a golden harp or a golden bowl of incense.

aliases: the sea of glass before the throne
payload.name: Heavenly throne room
payload.note: The heavenly court of God in Revelation, with the throne, elders, living creatures, the Lamb and the sea of glass before the throne.

stages.label: Heavenly throne room

quotes.quote: there was a throne set in heaven, and one sitting on the throne
the temple of the tabernacle of the testimony in heaven was opened
Lightnings, sounds, thunders, an earthquake, and great hail followed.

stages.text: Heavenly throne room: a vast open sanctuary of radiance beneath a heaven like crystal, floored with a sea of glass that is clear as crystal, set with a great throne and a temple whose doors open onto the heavens, lit by lightnings, thunders and a rainbow the colour of emerald about the throne. Pale gold and white stone, jasper and sardius glimmer in the walls; an altar of gold stands before the throne.

payload.title: Battle with Amalek; Moses' hands raised

payload.name: Hur
payload.note: Companion who holds up Moses' hands during the battle with Amalek and is left with Aaron to oversee disputes.

stages.label: Hur

quotes.quote: Aaron and Hur held up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side.

stages.text: Hur: man in his fifties to sixties, sturdy and weathered from desert travel; medium build with strong, steady arms; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked dark hair and a trimmed grey beard; calm, dignified face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain woven undertunic of undyed cream linen under a rust-brown wool cloak. No props.

payload.name: Joshua son of Nun
payload.note: Son of Nun of Ephraim, Moses' aide and successor who leads Israel into Canaan; the same individual across Exodus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges (as the deceased) and Hebrews, so no other Joshua is separated from him in this group.

stages.label: Joshua son of Nun

quotes.quote: Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, didn’t depart from the Tent.
Joshua was old and well advanced in years

stages.text: Joshua son of Nun: a man of mature strength in his prime, aged about forty to fifty when leading, with a sturdy, broad-shouldered build and weathered brown skin marked by desert sun. Short dark hair, close-cropped beard, steady deep-set eyes and a firm, grave face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic and a dark brown woven wool cloak. Carries a bronze-bladed sword at his belt and a long wooden spear.

payload.name: Amalekites
payload.note: The Amalekite people, an enemy nation that attacks Israel at Rephidim in Exodus, comes against Israel at Hormah in Numbers, and is recalled in Deuteronomy as the nation that struck Israel's weary rear; all three refer to the same people.

stages.label: Amalekites

quotes.quote: Then Amalek came and fought with Israel in Rephidim.
the Amalekites had made a raid on the South and on Ziklag, and had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire

stages.text: Amalekites: a typical warrior of a desert people, adult, aged roughly twenty-five to forty; lean, weathered build; sun-darkened olive-brown skin; dark hair tied back, short beard kept close; strong, wind-creased face with a steady gaze. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic belted with leather, over it a sand-coloured woven cloak in ochre and brown. Carries a curved sword at the belt and a leather shield as their own props.

payload.name: Rephidim
payload.note: Camp in Exodus where Israel struck the rock for water at Massah and Meribah and fought Amalek; the rock and battle story are specific to this site.

stages.label: Rephidim

quotes.quote: encamped in Rephidim; but there was no water for the people to drink.
Then Amalek came and fought with Israel in Rephidim.
they encamped in the wilderness; and there Israel encamped before the mountain.

stages.text: Rephidim: a wide, dry valley of pale sand and broken limestone in the Sinai wilderness, bordered by low, rust-coloured cliffs. A single great rock face of dark grey granite rises at the valley's head, its surface cracked and streaked with mineral stains. Sparse thorn scrub and tufts of dry grass grow in the gullies, with a few stunted acacia trees near the rock. Distant peaks of Sinai show as blue-grey shapes on the horizon.

payload.title: Water from the rock at Meribah

payload.name: Kadesh (Kadesh Barnea)
payload.note: Desert oasis of the spies, the rebellion and the water from the rock in Numbers, also called the wilderness of Zin.

stages.label: Kadesh (Kadesh Barnea)

quotes.quote: The people stayed in Kadesh. Miriam died there, and was buried there.
Behold, we are in Kadesh, a city in the edge of your border.
Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom

stages.text: Kadesh: a desert oasis in the wilderness of Zin at the edge of Edom's border, a wide basin of pale sand and gravel ringed by low rocky ridges. A spring wells from the rock beside a cluster of goat-hair tents and a few mud-brick walls of a settlement. Tamarisk, acacia and scattered palms grow near the water; beyond, the bare hills of the wilderness rise.

payload.title: Peter denies Jesus

payload.name: Crowd in Luke
payload.note: The mass of people following Jesus, hearing John and being healed throughout Luke.

stages.label: Crowd in Luke

quotes.quote: a great number of the people from all Judea and Jerusalem and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon
A great multitude of the people followed him, including women who also mourned and lamented him.

stages.text: Crowd in Luke: a typical member is an ordinary adult of Judean or Galilean village life, from young adult to middle age, lean and sun-worn, with olive or brown skin, dark hair kept short or tied back, and a short beard or clean-shaven face; plain undyed linen or wool tunic in ochre, undyed cream and earth brown, with a woollen cloak and a head covering; carries no props of their own.

aliases: the court of the high priest
the courtyard of the high priest
payload.name: the court of the high priest (Caiaphas)
payload.note: Courtyard of Caiaphas where Jesus is tried and Peter denies him in Matthew; same court as the high priest's court in John, identified by Caiaphas and the trial setting.

stages.label: The court of the high priest

quotes.quote: the court of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas
He was sitting with the officers, and warming himself in the light of the fire.
entered in with Jesus into the court of the high priest

stages.text: The court of the high priest: an open paved courtyard of pale limestone flagstones inside a high-walled stone house in Jerusalem. A wide arched gateway with a timber door faces the street. A charcoal fire burns on a stone hearth at the centre of the court, and a stone porch with columns stands along one side. Olive and fig trees grow in clay pots by the walls; the upper walls are plastered and lit by torch sconces.

payload.title: Healing of the lame man at the temple gate

payload.name: John the apostle, son of Zebedee
payload.note: Fisherman apostle, brother of James son of Zebedee, appearing in Matthew, Luke and Acts; distinct from John the Baptist and John Mark.

stages.label: John the apostle

quotes.quote: in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets
who were partners with Simon

stages.text: John the apostle: young man of about twenty-five to thirty; lean, strong fisherman's build; sun-browned skin; dark brown hair falling to the shoulders, short beard; clear, earnest eyes and a steady, youthful face. Signature outfit: plain undyed linen tunic in earth tones with a dark brown wool cloak, sleeves rolled. Carries a coiled fishing net over one shoulder.

payload.name: Crowd in Acts
payload.note: The crowd gathering in Jerusalem, Ephesus, Lystra and elsewhere to hear, mock or riot in Acts.

stages.label: Crowd in Acts

quotes.quote: the multitude came together and were bewildered, because everyone heard them speaking in his own language.
for the multitude of the people followed after, crying out, “Away with him!”

stages.text: Crowd in Acts: a typical member is an adult of about twenty to fifty years, lean and sun-browned from working outdoors, with dark brown or black hair worn short or tied back and beards kept short on men. Skin olive to tawny, faces weathered and serious. Clothing: a plain undyed linen tunic in ochre or earth-brown, a dark wool cloak in deep blue or grey, sandals. Carries no props of his own.

payload.name: the Jerusalem temple
payload.note: The single Jerusalem temple building across all five divisions (courts, porch and gates are parts of the same place), so every entry is one place.

stages.label: The Jerusalem temple

quotes.quote: Jesus entered into the temple of God and drove out all of those who sold and bought in the temple
The veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom.
the door of the temple which is called Beautiful
how it was decorated with beautiful stones and gifts
His disciples came to him to show him the buildings of the temple.

stages.text: The Jerusalem temple: a vast complex of white limestone and gleaming gold on a raised stone platform atop Mount Moriah. Wide colonnaded courts, a tall sanctuary house with a gilded roof, a great curtained veil within, a treasury chamber, and a Beautiful Gate of bronze. Olive trees and cedar frame the courts.

payload.title: Samuel anoints David at Bethlehem

payload.name: Samuel
payload.note: Son of Hannah raised at Shiloh, judge and prophet who anoints Saul and David; the child of Eli's temple, not Elkanah.

stages.label: Samuel as a boy at Shiloh

quotes.quote: The child was young.
The child served Yahweh before Eli the priest.
The child Samuel grew on, and increased in favor both with Yahweh and also with men.

stages.text: Samuel: a boy of about ten years, slight and sturdy, with warm brown skin, short dark curly hair and clear, attentive eyes. His signature outfit is a plain undyed linen tunic of pale ochre with a short linen ephod-style sash, bare feet. He carries no props.

stages.label: Samuel as judge and prophet

quotes.quote: Samuel judged the children of Israel in Mizpah.
Fill your horn with oil, and go.
Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.

stages.text: Samuel: a man in his middle years, lean and upright, with weathered brown skin, a close-trimmed dark beard flecked with grey, short hair and calm, steady eyes. His signature outfit is a long undyed linen tunic belted at the waist under a deep blue wool cloak. He carries a horn of oil at his belt and, on journeys, a plain wooden staff.

payload.name: Jesse
payload.note: Bethlehemite father of David and his seven sons.

stages.label: Jesse

quotes.quote: The man was an elderly old man in the days of Saul.
I will send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite

stages.text: Jesse: an elderly man of Bethlehem in Judah, past sixty, lean and upright from years of labour; olive-brown skin weathered by sun; short grey beard close to the jaw; grey hair under a plain head-cloth; deep lines around the eyes and a steady, serious face. Signature outfit: an undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown under a dark brown woollen cloak with a thick fringe at the hem. Carries a shepherd's staff of dark wood; no other props alone.

payload.name: Eliab
payload.note: Eldest son of Jesse, David's oldest brother, who is angry at him in the valley of Elah.

stages.label: Eliab, firstborn son of Jesse

quotes.quote: The three oldest sons of Jesse had gone after Saul to the battle
Eliab his oldest brother heard when he spoke to the men

stages.text: Eliab: man in his twenties, tall and broad-shouldered from years of shepherding and soldiering; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and a trimmed beard; strong brow, straight nose and a set, stern mouth. Signature outfit: a sleeveless tunic of undyed linen under a rust-red cloak, with bronze scale armor on the shoulders. Carries a round bronze shield and a short sword.

payload.name: Abinadab son of Jesse
payload.note: Jesse's second son passed over by Samuel at Bethlehem; distinct from the Kiriath Jearim host who keeps the ark.

stages.label: Abinadab son of Jesse
stages.text: Abinadab son of Jesse: man in his twenties; sturdy, broad-shouldered build; olive-brown skin; dark curly hair and short beard; steady, serious face with a strong nose. Signature outfit: undyed linen tunic with a plain blue-grey wool cloak. Carries no props alone.

payload.name: Shammah
payload.note: Son of Jesse passed over by Samuel; serves in Saul's army.

stages.label: Shammah

quotes.quote: Then Jesse made Shammah to pass by.
the third Shammah

stages.text: Shammah: a young man of about twenty, lean and sinewy from shepherding and soldiering; medium height; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard; calm, steady features with a serious, dignified bearing. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a deep ochre woollen cloak. Signature prop: a leather sling.

payload.name: Ramah of Benjamin (Ramathaim Zophim)
payload.note: Home city of Elkanah, Samuel's birthplace and seat of judgment in 1 Samuel; not the Baasha border town, and identified by the Samuel sections and the Ramathaim Zophim alias.

stages.label: Ramah of Benjamin

quotes.quote: a certain man of Ramathaim Zophim, of the hill country of Ephraim
he judged Israel there; and he built an altar to Yahweh there
came to the great well that is in Secu
under the tamarisk tree in Ramah

stages.text: Ramah of Benjamin: a hill town on a rocky ridge in the hill country, terraced slopes of olive and terebinth, low flat-roofed houses of mud brick and fieldstone, a stone altar of unhewn stones set on the high ground, a great well with a worn stone rim near the town's edge, a tamarisk tree standing in the open, and a little sanctuary of Naioth on the rise.

payload.title: David offers to fight Goliath

payload.name: Gibeah of Saul (1 Samuel)
payload.note: Saul's home town and royal seat in 1 Samuel, where Saul is found, anointed and later fights the Philistines at Michmash; distinguish from the Judges Gibeah by its link to Saul and the monarchy.

stages.label: Gibeah of Saul

quotes.quote: Saul also went to his house in Gibeah
under the pomegranate tree which is in Migron
Saul was sitting in Gibeah, under the tamarisk tree in Ramah

stages.text: Gibeah of Saul: a fortified hill town of Benjamin on a rocky ridge in the central highlands. Stone-walled terraces climb the slopes, flat-roofed houses of limestone and mudbrick cluster near a citadel tower at the crest, and a town gate faces the approach road. Terebinth and pomegranate trees grow at the edge of the upper town, with a tamarisk tree in the open ground below, and hills of scrub and olive fall away eastward toward the wilderness.

payload.title: Saul's jealousy and spear

payload.name: the evil spirit from God
payload.note: Spirit that troubles Saul and is eased by David's harp.

stages.label: The evil spirit from God

quotes.quote: Then when the evil spirit from God is on you, he will play with his hand, and you will be well.

stages.text: The evil spirit from God: no body or face, shown only as a dark, heavy shadow gathering about Saul's chamber, a cold wind that stirs the hangings and dims the lamplight, its edges sombre grey and bruised violet, faintly threaded with a dull ember glow.

payload.title: Daniel rebukes Belshazzar

payload.name: Belshazzar
payload.note: King of Babylon during the feast and handwriting on the wall; slain the same night.

stages.label: Belshazzar, king of Babylon

quotes.quote: Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords
his face was changed in him

stages.text: Belshazzar: a man in his thirties or early forties, of lean, upright build; olive-bronze skin; short dark hair and a neatly curled beard in the Mesopotamian royal manner; a strong brow and deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long fringed royal robe of deep crimson wool over a white linen tunic, with a tall, pleated, gold-banded crown. Carries a gold-hilted ceremonial dagger at the belt.

payload.name: Royal palace of Babylon
payload.note: Babylonian palace where the king receives counsel, sees the handwriting and hears Daniel's interpretations; distinct from the Susa palace.

stages.label: Royal palace of Babylon

quotes.quote: he was walking in the royal palace of Babylon

stages.text: Royal palace of Babylon: a vast walled complex on the flat alluvial plain of the Euphrates, built of sun-dried and fired brick glazed in deep blue with yellow lion and dragon reliefs. Tiered terraces rise toward a great gate with tall towers; hanging gardens of palms, date trees and climbing vines spill over the walls. Broad courts of pale stone lead to a banquet hall with high cedar-beamed ceilings and a river-facing colonnade.

payload.title: Laws of the burnt offering

aliases: the door of the Tent of Meeting
the court of the Tent of Meeting
payload.name: the tabernacle (portable sanctuary)
payload.note: The one portable sanctuary of the wilderness, described in Exodus 25-40 and referred to as the Tent of Meeting in Leviticus and Numbers; all three entries are the same place.

stages.label: The tabernacle (portable sanctuary)

quotes.quote: made the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twined linen, blue, purple, and scarlet. They made them with cherubim
He made curtains of goats’ hair for a covering over the tabernacle.
He made the boards for the tabernacle, twenty boards for the south side southward.
the sockets around the court, the sockets of the gate of the court, all the pins of the tabernacle
