stages.text: The tabernacle: a portable sanctuary of a rectangular tent of fine twined linen curtains in blue, purple and scarlet woven with cherubim, over a covering of goats' hair and rams' skins, stretched over upright acacia boards overlaid with gold, set in silver sockets and held by gold-covered bars, enclosed by a court of white linen hangings on bronze pillars.

payload.name: the altar
payload.note: The bronze altar at the door of the Tent of Meeting in Leviticus, where sacrifices are burned; not the Jerusalem temple.

stages.label: the altar

quotes.quote: the altar that is at the door of the Tent of Meeting
the horns of the altar of sweet incense before Yahweh
Fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it shall not go out.
He shall kill it on the north side of the altar before Yahweh.

stages.text: the altar: a square hearth of acacia wood overlaid with bronze, set in an open courtyard before the tent door, with projecting horns at its four corners and a fire burning continually upon it; a bronze basin and its base stand near; the ground at its base is worn and ash-grey; a tent of linen hangings rises behind it in the desert.

payload.title: Daniel cast into the den
Wisdom's public call and her worth

payload.name: Wisdom
payload.note: The personified figure Lady Wisdom who calls in the streets, builds a seven-pillared house, and speaks in Proverbs 1, 3, 4, 8 and 9; not a human woman.

stages.label: Wisdom as radiant presence

quotes.quote: Beside the gates, at the entry of the city, at the entry doors, she cries aloud:
Wisdom has built her house. She has carved out her seven pillars.

stages.text: Wisdom: no human face or body; she is shown only as radiance, a pale luminous brightness gathered like light at a city gate, unbounded and warm. Her presence is light and voice, never a figure to be drawn as a woman.

aliases: the high places of the city
payload.name: The streets and city gates
payload.note: Public squares and gates of a city where Wisdom cries out and judgment is given; distinct from Jerusalem as a named city.

stages.label: The streets and city gates

quotes.quote: Wisdom calls aloud in the street. She utters her voice in the public squares.
Beside the gates, at the entry of the city, at the entry doors, she cries aloud:
She sits at the door of her house, on a seat in the high places of the city,

stages.text: The streets and city gates: a walled town of packed earth and mudbrick and dressed stone on a low hill, with a broad double city gate of cedar-banded timber set in thick stone towers. Beyond the gate the public square is paved with flat limestone slabs, worn pale by feet. Mud-plastered houses of two storeys line narrow lanes; flat roofs, lintels, and stone benches stand by the gate. Olive trees and terraced vines grow on the slopes, with a tall high place of cut stone above the square.

payload.title: The hymn of love

payload.name: The Corinthian believers
payload.note: The quarrelling assembly at Corinth addressed by Paul in 1 Corinthians; addressees rather than a stage group.

stages.label: The Corinthian believers

quotes.quote: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
For it has been reported to me concerning you, my brothers, by those who are from Chloe’s household, that there are contentions among you.
For though you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, you don’t have many fathers.

stages.text: The Corinthian believers: a typical member is an adult of thirty to fifty years, of mixed Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean stock, with olive or light brown skin weathered by sea air and street life. Hair is dark or brown, worn short or tied back, with a clean-shaven or short-bearded face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic in ochre with a dark brown woollen cloak. Carries no props alone.

payload.name: Corinth
payload.note: The Greek city of Corinth, the setting of Paul's eighteen-month ministry in Acts, the church addressed in 1 and 2 Corinthians, and the place mentioned in Romans and 2 Timothy; all entries refer to the same city.

stages.label: Corinth

quotes.quote: After these things Paul departed from Athens and came to Corinth.

stages.text: Corinth: a Greek and Roman port city on a broad isthmus between two seas, with a steep citadel rising behind it. Limestone and brick houses and shops line straight streets; a stone forum with colonnaded porticoes, temples and a theatre stand at its centre. Olive groves, vines and pine trees cover the slopes beyond the walls.

payload.title: Incomparable God and the strength of the waiting

aliases: the city of my fathers' tombs
payload.name: Jerusalem
payload.note: The capital city of Judah (also called Jebus, David's city, the holy city, Zion as city in some books); the city itself, distinct from the hill/mountain of Zion as a place of Yahweh's dwelling.

stages.label: Jerusalem

quotes.quote: they buried him in David's city
a breach was made in the city

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs crowd the slopes; a fortified citadel of the stronghold of Zion stands on the high ground. Massive city walls with gates, and above the city the temple mount crowned by a stone-built temple of Yahweh.

payload.title: Recollection of Horeb and the failed spy mission

payload.name: Caleb son of Jephunneh
payload.note: Judahite spy who urges entering Canaan, and the man who offers Achsah at Kiriath Sepher in Judges.

stages.label: Caleb

quotes.quote: Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him

stages.text: Caleb: a strong man in his prime, middle-aged and weathered by desert travel, of medium-to-tall build with broad shoulders. Warm brown skin, short dark hair and a close-cut beard touched with early grey. Calm, steady face with deep-set eyes and a firm mouth. Wears a woven undyed wool tunic under a long cloak of deep earth-red, with a linen head-wrap. Carries a plain wooden staff; no other signature prop.

aliases: the mountain that might be touched
payload.name: Horeb/Mount Sinai
payload.note: The single mountain of God where the law and covenant are given; all listed entries (Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, Malachi, Hebrews) refer to the same mountain under the names Horeb, Sinai, God's mountain, referenced across divisions.

stages.label: Horeb/Mount Sinai

quotes.quote: All of Mount Sinai smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire
You shall set bounds to the people all around
the cloud covered it six days
The mountain burned with fire to the heart of the sky, with darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.

stages.text: Horeb/Mount Sinai: a single steep granite mountain rising from a stark desert wilderness of rock and sand; its lower slopes are broken boulders and gravel, its upper peak sharp and dark, with a cloud-wrapped summit. The base is marked by a rocky plain where the people camp, bounded by stones. No vegetation beyond scattered desert shrub; the mountain has no buildings.

payload.name: The plains of Moab
payload.note: Eastern camp across the Jordan where Moses speaks the law and dies, Deuteronomy only.

stages.label: The plains of Moab

quotes.quote: Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to declare this law
Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is opposite Jericho.
in the valley opposite Beth Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites

stages.text: The plains of Moab: a broad, low valley of dry grassland and scrub east of the Jordan, opposite Jericho and Beth Peor, with acacia, tamarisk and wild shrubs along the river line. Rising to the west, the bare slopes of Mount Nebo and Pisgah, with a flat-topped summit, look over the Jordan valley. Plain tents of goat hair and rough stone walls mark the Israelite encampment; no buildings of note stand in the valley.

payload.title: The builders assign the gates and sections

payload.name: Eliashib
payload.note: High priest in Jerusalem who helps rebuild the sheep gate, later gives Tobiah a room in the temple; grandfather line of Joiada's son.

stages.label: Eliashib, high priest

quotes.quote: Then Eliashib the high priest rose up with his brothers the priests
Eliashib the priest, who was appointed over the rooms of the house of our God

stages.text: Eliashib: a man in his fifties, broad-shouldered and dignified; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked dark beard and close-cropped hair; lined brow and steady, serious eyes. Signature outfit: white linen priestly tunic and sash with a blue-violet robe over it, and the high priest's linen turban with a gold plate. Carries no props alone.

payload.name: the priests (group)
payload.note: The priestly class of the sons of Aaron who perform the rites of offering in Leviticus and who repair gates, take part in processions and sign the covenant in Nehemiah; both entries are the same priestly body, so they are one cluster.

stages.label: the priests (group)

quotes.quote: Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall present the blood
and some of the priests’ sons with trumpets

stages.text: The priests: adult men, mostly between thirty and fifty, sturdy and unhurried in bearing. Olive to deep bronze skin, short dark or greying beard, close-cropped hair under a linen head covering. Calm, dignified faces. Signature outfit: a white linen tunic and sash, with a plain linen mitre, in cream and off-white. Props: a bronze censer or a trumpet for processional scenes.

payload.name: the sheep gate
payload.note: Gate of Jerusalem the priests begin repairing first, near the tower of Hananel.

stages.label: The Sheep Gate

quotes.quote: they built the sheep gate. They sanctified it, and set up its doors.
even to the tower of Hammeah, to the tower of Hananel.

stages.text: The Sheep Gate: a plain gateway cut through the northern wall of Jerusalem, built of rough-hewn limestone blocks with a low stone arch and heavy timber doors bound in bronze, set between squared towers of the restored wall. Dry grey hillside, scattered terebinth and olive trees, and the pale stone of the old city rising beyond.

aliases: the wide place before the water gate
payload.name: the water gate
payload.note: Open square and gate where Ezra reads the law to the assembly.

stages.label: The water gate

quotes.quote: into the wide place that was in front of the water gate
the place opposite the water gate toward the east, and the tower that stands out

stages.text: The water gate: an open, paved square fronting a stone gateway in the eastern wall of Jerusalem, near the Ophel and the projecting tower. Rough-hewn limestone blocks, pale ochre and grey, form the wall and arched gate passage; the square is worn flagstone with a low stone bench along the wall. Sparse olive trees and a few palms grow beyond the wall toward the Kidron valley.

payload.title: Hezekiah's reforms and tithes

aliases: king of Judah son of Ahaz
payload.name: Hezekiah
payload.note: Reforming king of Judah son of Ahaz who receives Isaiah.

stages.label: Hezekiah, king of Judah

quotes.quote: Hezekiah began to reign when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem.
And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
When King Hezekiah heard it, he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into Yahweh’s house.

stages.text: Hezekiah: a man in his late twenties to forties, lean and upright, of Israelite stock. Olive-brown skin, close-trimmed dark beard, dark hair pinned under a royal fillet. Grave, weathered face. Signature outfit: a long undertunic of undyed linen under a deep-blue royal court robe with a woven gold border. Signature prop: a plain wooden royal staff.

payload.title: Guidance by the cloud and fire
Holmes's deductions on Watson's marriage

aliases: the old man by the brazier
payload.name: Sherlock Holmes
payload.note: Consulting detective of Baker Street, Watson's friend and the investigator in every division of this group, who disguises himself variously; appears across all stories.

stages.label: Sherlock Holmes

quotes.quote: He was, I take it, the most perfect reasoning and observing machine that the world has seen
tweed-suited and respectable, as of old

stages.text: Sherlock Holmes: a man of about thirty-five, tall and lean, with an angular face, high cheekbones and a strong, square jaw; short dark-brown hair, side-parted and swept back at the sides; heavy, straight dark brows over keen grey eyes; a straight, high-bridged nose; clean-shaven. Bareheaded. Wears a dark Victorian frock coat over a brown waistcoat, a high white collar and a dark cravat. Carries a clay pipe and a magnifying glass.

payload.name: Dr. Watson
payload.note: Narrator and Holmes's companion, a doctor and chronicler, present in every story of this group.

stages.label: Dr. Watson

quotes.quote: I think, Watson, that you have put on seven and a half pounds since I saw you.
I am lost without my Boswell.

stages.text: Dr. Watson: a man in his thirties of middle height, strongly built with broad shoulders, a thick neck and a square jaw; weathered, ruddy complexion from army service; brown hair parted at the side and brushed flat; a full, heavy, dark-brown moustache; steady, open face. Wears a dark wool frock coat, grey waistcoat, white collar and dark tie, with a bowler hat. Carries a physician's black bag.

payload.name: Holmes's rooms, Baker Street
payload.note: Holmes and Watson's lodgings where the case is discussed and the King visits.

stages.label: Holmes's rooms, Baker Street

quotes.quote: His rooms were brilliantly lit
remained in our lodgings in Baker Street, buried among his old books
I sat down beside the fire

stages.text: Holmes's rooms, Baker Street: a tall brick terraced house in a London street, with a well-kept front door, and upper-floor sitting rooms whose tall sash windows glow with lamplight at dusk. Inside, a coal fire burns in the grate, with a worn carpet, shelves of old books, a desk heaped with papers, and a chemical table by the window.

payload.title: The masked visitor arrives

payload.name: Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond von Ormstein, King of Bohemia
payload.note: Hereditary King of Bohemia, visiting London incognito under the name Count Von Kramm; masked client who hires Holmes to recover a photograph of himself with Irene Adler.

stages.label: The King of Bohemia, as Count Von Kramm

quotes.quote: The Count shrugged his broad shoulders.
he tore the mask from his face and hurled it upon the ground
took a heavy chamois leather bag from under his cloak

stages.text: Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond von Ormstein: a man in his thirties, broad-shouldered and heavily built; fair skin, short fair hair and a close-trimmed moustache; strong, aristocratic features; a black half-mask hides his eyes and upper face. Signature outfit: a dark wool travelling cloak over a dark frock coat and waistcoat, with a high white collar. Props: a heavy chamois leather bag of gold.

payload.title: Wilson's visit to Holmes

payload.name: Jabez Wilson
payload.note: Stout, florid, red-headed pawnbroker of Saxe-Coburg Square, the client who brings the Red-headed League case to Holmes.

stages.label: Jabez Wilson

quotes.quote: The portly client puffed out his chest with an appearance of some little pride
He wore rather baggy grey shepherd’s check trousers, a not over-clean black frock-coat, unbuttoned in the front, and a drab waistcoat with a heavy brassy Albert chain
there was nothing remarkable about the man save his blazing red head, and the expression of extreme chagrin and discontent upon his features.

stages.text: Jabez Wilson: a stout, pompous pawnbroker of middle age, obese and slow in build, with fair English skin reddened about the face. His hair is a blazing, fiery red, and he has a close-cut red beard. Florid cheeks and a discontented, chagrined expression. Signature outfit: baggy grey shepherd's check trousers, a not over-clean black frock-coat, and a drab waistcoat with a heavy brassy Albert chain and a square pierced metal ornament.

payload.name: Baker Street
payload.note: Holmes's rooms where the opening consultation and the late-night gathering take place.

stages.label: Baker Street rooms

quotes.quote: Two hansoms were standing at the door, and as I entered the passage I heard the sound of voices from above.
as we sat over a glass of whisky and soda in Baker Street

stages.text: Baker Street rooms: a Marylebone street of tall brick terraces with stuccoed fronts, sash windows and iron railings, lamps on iron posts; the rooms lie up a narrow passage and staircase from the street door, with a sitting room of worn furniture, a desk, a coal fire, bookshelves and newspapers.

payload.title: Holmes examines the pawnshop and the bank

payload.name: Saxe-Coburg Square
payload.note: Small shabby square in the City where Wilson's pawnbroker shop stands.

stages.label: Saxe-Coburg Square

quotes.quote: a poky, little, shabby-genteel place, where four lines of dingy two-storied brick houses looked out into a small railed-in enclosure
a lawn of weedy grass and a few clumps of faded laurel bushes made a hard fight against a smoke-laden and uncongenial atmosphere
Three gilt balls and a brown board with “JABEZ WILSON” in white letters, upon a corner house

stages.text: Saxe-Coburg Square: a small, shabby-genteel square in the City of London, near Aldersgate. Four lines of dingy two-storied brick terrace houses face a small railed-in enclosure of weedy grass and a few clumps of faded laurel bushes struggling in smoky air. On a corner house, three gilt pawnbroker's balls and a brown board lettered JABEZ WILSON in white. Gas lamps, worn pavement, soot-stained brick.

payload.name: the main City road near Saxe-Coburg Square
payload.note: Crowded commercial thoroughfare running past the back of Saxe-Coburg Square.

stages.label: Main City road, Victorian commercial thoroughfare
stages.text: The main City road: a wide, busy commercial thoroughfare of grey stone and soot-darkened brick warehouses, banks and shopfronts, with iron gas lamps, tramlines set in cobbles, and tall chimneys in the distance. Plane trees line the pavement in patches, and a few narrow side lanes branch off toward the square.

payload.title: Holmes reads the hat

payload.name: Baker Street sitting-room
payload.note: Holmes's rooms, where the hat is examined, the stone kept, and the final confrontation takes place.

stages.label: Baker Street sitting-room

quotes.quote: the bright semicircle which was thrown from the fanlight
we were shown up together to Holmes’ room
we were back in the sitting-room at Baker Street

stages.text: Baker Street sitting-room: a first-floor room in a plain brick Baker Street terrace, reached by a steep staircase from the street door beneath a semicircular fanlight. Tall sash windows overlook the street, with heavy curtains. A coal fire burns in a grate beneath a plain mantelpiece; a desk and shelves of papers and books line the walls, with a gasolier overhead.

payload.title: The whistle and the cry

payload.name: the swamp adder
payload.note: Venomous snake trained by Roylott to crawl down the bell-rope; killed Julia and then Roylott. Seen on stage at the end.

stages.label: the swamp adder

quotes.quote: The speckled band!
The idea of a snake instantly occurred to me
I heard the creature hiss

stages.text: the swamp adder: a venomous Indian snake about four feet long, thick-bodied and muscular, with smooth dry scales in dull yellow-brown ground marked by irregular dark blotches and bands of cream, giving it a speckled look; a broad flattened head with two small dark fangs, and cold watchful eyes.

aliases: the room in which my sister died
payload.name: Helen's bedroom
payload.note: The room where Julia died, with the dummy bell-rope and the ventilator to Roylott's room.

stages.label: Helen's bedroom
stages.text: Helen's bedroom: a plain upper room in a rambling old country house at Stoke Moran, with whitewashed plaster walls, a narrow iron bedstead, a worn wooden floor and a small coal grate. A bell-rope hangs beside the bed, its end lying loose. High on the wall near the bed a ventilator opens into the adjoining room. Tall sash window, heavy curtains.

payload.title: Holmes outlines the case on the train

payload.name: the train to the west
payload.note: Railway journey from Paddington through Reading, Swindon and the Severn valley to Ross.

stages.label: the train to the west

quotes.quote: We had the carriage to ourselves save for an immense litter of papers
he suddenly rolled them all into a gigantic ball and tossed them up onto the rack.
rattling away to Paddington Station.

stages.text: the train to the west: a Great Western compartment carriage of varnished teak panelling, upholstered bench seats in dark green plush, brass luggage racks high above the seats, and framed windows with brass fittings. Beyond the glass, river meadows, hedgerows and the Thames valley slide past.

payload.title: Waiting in the bank cellar

payload.name: Peter Jones
payload.note: Official police agent from Scotland Yard, consequential and brave, who arrests Clay.

stages.label: Peter Jones

quotes.quote: the deeper, heavier in-breath of the bulky Jones
in his consequential way
as brave as a bulldog and as tenacious as a lobster

stages.text: Peter Jones: middle-aged, stout and heavy-set, with a broad, bulky frame and a self-important bearing. Ruddy, weathered skin, close-cropped sandy-grey hair, neat side-whiskers and a clean-shaven upper lip. Heavy, florid features with small, shrewd eyes. Signature outfit: a dark wool frock-coat and waistcoat of charcoal grey, a stiff white collar, and a dark bowler hat. Carries a stout oak truncheon at his belt alone.

payload.name: Mr. Merryweather
payload.note: Long, thin, sad-faced bank director and chairman, who worries about the French gold in the cellar.

stages.label: Mr. Merryweather

quotes.quote: observed Mr. Merryweather gloomily.
the thin, sighing note of the bank director
striking his stick upon the flags

stages.text: Mr. Merryweather: man in his fifties or sixties; tall, long-limbed and thin; pale, drawn, mournful face with deep lines; grey hair and neatly trimmed grey side-whiskers; clean-shaven upper lip. Dark wool frock coat over a waistcoat, high collar and dark cravat, the dress of a bank director; a dark hat. He carries a stout walking stick. Only the stick is his own prop.

payload.name: Cellar of the City and Suburban Bank
payload.note: Huge vault beneath the City branch bank where the napoleons are stored and the criminals' tunnel emerges.

stages.label: Cellar of the City and Suburban Bank

quotes.quote: We are at present, Doctor—as no doubt you have divined—in the cellar of the City branch of one of the principal London banks.
the cold dank air of the vault
The cellar! There was the end of this tangled clue.

stages.text: Cellar of the City and Suburban Bank: a vast low vault of old London brickwork beneath a bank branch in the City, with dank cold air, stone flags underfoot, and a tunnel mouth dug through the wall. Stacked wooden cases of coin stand in rows; gaslight and lantern fittings hang from the arches.

payload.title: The burning house and the aftermath

payload.name: Victor Hatherley
payload.note: Young hydraulic engineer, orphan and bachelor, who arrives at Watson's consulting-room with a severed thumb and recounts his night at Eyford; the narrator's patient and Holmes' client.

stages.label: Victor Hatherley

quotes.quote: the other was so strange in its inception and so dramatic in its details
Mr. Victor Hatherley, hydraulic engineer, 16A, Victoria Street (3rd floor).

stages.text: Victor Hatherley: young man in his mid twenties; slight to middling build; fair skin, pale from strain; short light-brown hair parted neatly; clean-shaven with a fine, serious face; a bandaged left hand. Signature outfit: a dark grey wool frock coat over a waistcoat and white collar, the coat worn at the collar. Carries no props of his own.

payload.name: Inspector Bradstreet
payload.note: Scotland Yard inspector who accompanies Holmes and Hatherley to Eyford and studies the ordnance map.

stages.label: Inspector Bradstreet

quotes.quote: Inspector Bradstreet, of Scotland Yard, a plain-clothes man
Bradstreet had spread an ordnance map of the county out upon the seat and was busy with his compasses

stages.text: Inspector Bradstreet: man in his forties; sturdy, medium build; fair skin weathered by outdoor work; short greying-brown hair, neatly parted; clean-shaven apart from a trim moustache; alert grey eyes and a broad, good-humoured face. Signature outfit: a dark grey wool frock coat over a waistcoat, with a dark four-in-hand tie and a black bowler hat. Carries an ordnance map, brass compasses and a pencil.

payload.name: the station-master
payload.note: Station-master at Eyford who reports the fire at Dr. Becher's house.

stages.label: the station-master

quotes.quote: The station-master laughed heartily.
“Yes, sir!” said the station-master.

stages.text: The station-master: a stout, hearty man in his fifties, broad-shouldered and ruddy-cheeked from outdoor work, with clean-shaven jowls and short greying side-whiskers. Dark blue railway uniform coat with brass buttons and a peaked cap, a waistcoat beneath, and a watch chain across his belly. Carries a lantern and a railway timetable.

payload.name: Eyford Station
payload.note: Small village station near Eyford, Berkshire, where Hatherley arrives and later wakes.

stages.label: Eyford Station

quotes.quote: reached the little dim-lit station after eleven o’clock
As I passed out through the wicket gate
It is a good seven miles from Eyford Station.
a small clump of trees in the neighbourhood

stages.text: Eyford Station: a small rural station in Berkshire, a single short platform of old brick and timber under a plain pitched roof, with a low lamp post and a dim-lit waiting shelter. A wooden wicket gate opens onto a narrow lane. Surrounding country is flat, open fields and hedgerows of hawthorn, with scattered oaks and a dark clump of trees beyond. Nearby stands a quiet village of brick cottages.

payload.name: Eyford house
payload.note: The isolated whitewashed house near Eyford in Berkshire where the press is, which later burns down.

stages.label: Eyford house

quotes.quote: the bumping of the road was exchanged for the crisp smoothness of a gravel-drive
a porch which gaped in front of us
It was pitch dark inside the house

stages.text: Eyford house: an isolated two-storey rural house of whitewashed brick set back from a country road, reached by a smooth gravel drive. A deep porch shelters the front door, opening onto a dark hall and a long passage with rooms off it. Sash windows, slate roof, a few bare trees and rough hedgerows surround it, with flat fields of farmland beyond.

payload.title: The note, the hotel bill, and Lestrade's departure

payload.name: Lestrade
payload.note: Lean, ferret-like Scotland Yard detective who works the Boscombe Valley case at Ross; the Lestrade of the Boscombe and Noble Bachelor divisions.

stages.label: Lestrade

quotes.quote: A lean, ferret-like man, furtive and sly-looking
light brown dustcoat and leather-leggings
pea-jacket and cravat, which gave him a decidedly nautical appearance, and he carried a black canvas bag in his hand

stages.text: Lestrade: middle-aged English detective of Scotland Yard; lean, wiry build; pale, weathered skin; thinning sandy hair, close-cropped; narrow, sharp, ferret-like face with furtive, sly eyes and a thin mouth; clean-shaven or with a small moustache. Signature outfit: light brown dustcoat and leather leggings in the country, a navy pea-jacket and cravat in town; a black canvas bag carried in hand.

payload.name: Baker Street lodgings
payload.note: Holmes and Watson's shared rooms in Baker Street, where the client consultation and later supper take place.

stages.label: Baker Street lodgings

quotes.quote: With my body in one easy-chair and my legs upon another
our humble lodging-house mahogany

stages.text: Baker Street lodgings: a sitting room on the first floor of a tall brick terrace in London, with tall sash windows looking onto a narrow street of soot-darkened brick. Mahogany table and sideboard, worn easy-chairs with cushions, a coal fire in a black iron grate, bookshelves and a writing desk stacked with newspapers and papers. Gaslight and lamps, plain papered walls, a few framed prints.

payload.title: The stone's history and the advertisement
Holmes reads clues from Mary and the letters

payload.name: Holmes's lodgings at Baker Street
payload.note: Holmes's rooms where the consultations and the final confrontation take place.

stages.label: Holmes's lodgings at Baker Street

quotes.quote: his lodgings at Baker Street
we sat on either side of the fire
fly out of that window
a formidable array of bottles and test-tubes
the pungent cleanly smell of hydrochloric acid

stages.text: Holmes's lodgings at Baker Street: first-floor rooms in a tall brick Victorian terrace on a busy London street, with a sash window looking over slate roofs and chimney pots. A coal fire burns in the grate beside two armchairs, one deep and worn with a recess beside it. A cluttered desk, shelves of books and newspapers, and a chemistry table of bottles and test-tubes.

payload.title: The little door and the DRINK ME bottle

payload.name: Alice
payload.note: The protagonist, a curious little girl who falls down the rabbit-hole into Wonderland; every entry in this group is the same individual across all divisions, so there is no other Alice to separate from her.

stages.label: Alice

quotes.quote: the bright eager eyes were looking up into hers
that queer little toss of her head to keep back the wandering hair
How am I to get in?

stages.text: Alice: a young Victorian English girl of about seven, slight and small-boned, who grows very tall and shrinks very small over the course of her adventures. Skin fair with a light sunburn; long straight light-brown hair that often falls loose into her eyes, which she tosses back with a little shake of her head; bright, eager, curious features. Signature outfit: a pale yellow Victorian child's frock with short puffed sleeves and a sky-blue sash, a white pinafore with frilled shoulder straps, blue-and-white striped stockings and black strap shoes. Carries no props of her own.

payload.name: The long hall
payload.note: The one long, low hall with locked doors, the golden key, the three-legged glass table and the small curtained door; both entries describe this same hall in different sections, where Alice grows tall, shrinks and weeps.

stages.label: The long hall

quotes.quote: a long, low hall, which was lit up by a row of lamps hanging from the roof
There were doors all round the hall, but they were all locked
a little three-legged table, all made of solid glass
a low curtain she had not noticed before, and behind it was a little door about fifteen inches high
until there was a large pool all round her, about four inches deep and reaching half down the hall

stages.text: The long hall: a long, low hall lit by a row of lamps hanging from the roof, its floor and walls of worn grey stone with dark timber, lined on both sides with many tall locked doors. Near the middle stands a small three-legged table of solid glass, and beside it a low curtain hides a little door about fifteen inches high. Shallow salt water pools across the floor.

payload.title: The Caterpillar's Questions

payload.name: the Caterpillar
payload.note: The large blue caterpillar on a mushroom smoking a hookah, who questions Alice and gives her the mushroom advice; the third entry is only a back-reference to this same Caterpillar, so all three entries are one individual.

stages.label: the Caterpillar

quotes.quote: a large blue caterpillar, that was sitting on the top with its arms folded, quietly smoking a long hookah
rearing itself upright as it spoke (it was exactly three inches high)

stages.text: the Caterpillar: An adult caterpillar of large size with a caterpillar's segmented, many-legged body in a rich blue, its head an animal face with large, sleepy eyes. Human-like posture with folded arms when seated, and a long hookah pipe in its mouth. It sits atop a round mushroom and is exactly three inches tall when upright. Its manner is languid and sleepy.

payload.name: the mushroom
payload.note: The large mushroom in the wood where the Caterpillar sits; its two halves change size.  Scene of the conversation and the first nibbling.

stages.label: The mushroom

quotes.quote: as it was perfectly round, she found this a very difficult question
One side will make you grow taller, and the other side will make you grow shorter.

stages.text: The mushroom: a single very large, perfectly round toadstool growing in a wooded glade, its broad domed cap standing above a thick central stalk. Its cap is a rich mottled red-brown with pale spots, and its underside is pale cream. Grass and fallen leaves surround the base, and tall wood trees rise beyond it. The two opposite halves of its edge, one bright and one dark, are the parts that make things grow taller or shorter. No people or animals are in the scene.

payload.title: Quarrel over the crowded table and the riddle

payload.name: March Hare
payload.note: The anthropomorphic hare who hosts the mad tea party, lives in the large house Alice approaches, and later sits with the Hatter and Dormouse at the trial; all three entries are the same hare.

stages.label: March Hare

quotes.quote: lives a March Hare. Visit either you like: they're both mad.
the chimneys were shaped like ears and the roof was thatched with fur
the March Hare and the Hatter were having tea at it

stages.text: March Hare: an anthropomorphic hare with a hare's face, long upright ears and whiskers, human posture, standing in a lean adult build. Fur is pale brown-grey with darker tufts at the ears. Wears a Victorian waistcoat in faded green over a shirt with a loose cravat, and a rumpled tweed jacket. Signature prop: a teacup held in one paw, carried alone.

payload.name: The Hatter
payload.note: The Mad Hatter of Wonderland, seen at the mad tea party, mentioned by the Cat, and testifying as the first witness at the trial; the one individual across all three entries, with no conflicting notes to separate them.

stages.label: The Hatter

quotes.quote: the March Hare and the Hatter were having tea at it
He came in with a teacup in one hand and a piece of bread-and-butter in the other.
I keep them to sell,” the Hatter added as an explanation; “I’ve none of my own. I’m a hatter.”

stages.text: The Hatter: an adult man of middle age, lean and slightly stooped, with pale skin, untidy light-brown hair and a sparse beard, and a worried, anxious face with wide eyes. Signature outfit: a rumpled period frock coat and waistcoat in faded brown and mustard, with a battered tall top hat in faded green with a paper or ribbon band. Signature props: a teacup and a piece of bread-and-butter, and a pocket watch he shakes and holds to his ear.

payload.name: The Dormouse
payload.note: The sleepy dormouse of the Hatter and Hare at the mad tea-party, who tells the treacle-well story and later testifies sleepily at the trial; both entries are the same animal, so tell it apart from no other dormouse in this group.

stages.label: The Dormouse

quotes.quote: a Dormouse was sitting between them, fast asleep
in a hoarse, feeble voice
Off with his whiskers!

stages.text: The Dormouse: a small dormouse with a round soft-furred face, small round ears, a pale grey-brown coat, long whiskers and drowsy half-closed eyes, standing upright in human posture and wearing a plain waistcoat and small shabby jacket. Hoarse, feeble voice; he is perpetually sleepy and is often pinched awake.

aliases: the table in front of the house
payload.name: Tea table under the tree
payload.note: Long table set out under a tree in front of a house in the wood, laid with tea things, where the tea party takes place.

stages.label: Tea table under the tree

quotes.quote: There was a table set out under a tree in front of the house
The table was a large one, but the three were all crowded together at one corner of it
there was nothing on it but tea

stages.text: Tea table under the tree: a long table set out under a broad tree in a clearing in the wood, in front of a small house. The table is large and laid with a cloth and many cups, saucers, a teapot and a milk-jug, with bread-and-butter, and it is crowded with tea things at one corner. Tall grass and wild wood surround the clearing, and the tree's spreading branches shade the table.

payload.title: The Rabbit's whisper and the game

aliases: the White Rabbit with pink eyes
payload.name: White Rabbit
payload.note: The talking white rabbit (called the Rabbit) who runs late with a pocket watch, flees from Alice, mistakes her for Mary Ann, and later serves as the court herald and official reading the verses; all entries describe this one rabbit across the divisions.

stages.label: White Rabbit

quotes.quote: a White Rabbit with pink eyes ran close by her
the Rabbit actually _took a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket_
with a pair of white kid gloves in one hand and a large fan in the other
Oh my ears and whiskers, how late it’s getting!

stages.text: White Rabbit: an anthropomorphic white rabbit with a rabbit's face, long white ears, pink eyes, and whiskers, standing upright with human posture. Adult, nervous and fussy in build, slight and small. Soft white fur with pink inner ears. Wears a waistcoat with a pocket holding a pocket watch and a fine Victorian coat. Signature props alone: a pocket watch, a pair of white kid gloves, and a large fan.

payload.name: The Queen of Hearts
payload.note: The one tyrannical Queen of Hearts, the King's wife, who sends the croquet invitation, orders executions and presides at the croquet game and the trial; all five entries are her, with no conflicting portrayal, so they form one cluster.

stages.label: The Queen of Hearts

quotes.quote: The Queen turned crimson with fury
Here the Queen put on her spectacles
last of all this grand procession, came THE KING AND QUEEN OF HEARTS.

stages.text: The Queen of Hearts: a flat, oblong playing card with a head, arms and legs, drawn like the queen on a Victorian court card: a heavy-jawed, scowling woman of middle age with an ordinary fair face and dark hair drawn neatly under a small gold crown. Her card body is printed with a stiff court-card robe in red, gold and blue with heart motifs. Her signature prop is a rounded golden sceptre held in one hand.

payload.name: the King of Hearts
payload.note: The single timid King of Hearts, husband of the Queen, who pardons the condemned at the croquet game and presides as judge at the trial; all four entries are the same king across divisions.

stages.label: The King of Hearts

quotes.quote: as he wore his crown over the wig, (look at the frontispiece if you want to see how he did it,) he did not look at all comfortable
The King turned pale, and shut his note-book hastily.

stages.text: The King of Hearts: an elderly, mild, timid man of about sixty with a short grey-white beard and a mild, anxious face, wearing a tall gold crown set over a great white judge's wig and round spectacles. A flat, oblong playing-card body with head, arms and legs at the corners, printed with a long crimson royal robe with ermine trim and red hearts. Carries a small sceptre and a note-book.

payload.name: Cheshire Cat
payload.note: The grinning talking cat that speaks in riddles, says everyone is mad, and vanishes and reappears; appears in the kitchen, the wood, and the croquet ground, and is distinct from Dinah, Alice's home cat.

stages.label: Cheshire Cat

quotes.quote: It's a Cheshire cat
beginning with the end of the tail, and ending with the grin, which remained some time after the rest of it had gone

stages.text: Cheshire Cat: a large grinning cat with an animal face and a wide, broad-lipped grin, long sharp claws, and many teeth. Its fur is striped in soft grey and ginger with paler muzzle and chest. Its build is lean and long-bodied, with a long curling tail. It has no dress; its signature feature is the wide grin, which can hang in the air after the rest of it has gone.

payload.name: The Queen's card soldiers
payload.note: The Queen's card soldiers who march in the procession, form arches on the croquet-ground and take players into custody; told apart from the court officers by their croquet-ground and arch duties.

stages.label: The Queen's card soldiers

quotes.quote: First came ten soldiers carrying clubs; these were all shaped like the three gardeners, oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners
the soldiers had to double themselves up and to stand on their hands and feet, to make the arches

stages.text: The Queen's card soldiers: flat, oblong playing-card figures with a head, arms and legs, hands and feet at the corners of the card, a club-suit pattern on the body, carrying clubs. Dressed in simple card-soldier livery of red and white, with a plain round cap and a club emblem on the tabard. Their stiff card bodies are uniform and identical in build.

payload.name: the croquet players
payload.note: The guests and players in the Queen's croquet game who play all at once, quarrel over the hedgehogs, and are condemned then pardoned by the King; the same group under both the Queen's croquet ground and the Mock Turtle's story.

stages.label: the croquet players

quotes.quote: The players all played at once without waiting for turns, quarrelling all the while
all the players, except the King, the Queen, and Alice, were in custody

stages.text: the croquet players: a group of flat, oblong playing-card figures, each a card with a head, arms and legs and no card tunic, the typical member about a card's height in a stiff, slightly crumpled card body with a painted face, small arms and legs, shown as a Victorian-era court card in faded red and black ink, a wide-eyed bewildered look on the face, and carrying a croquet mallet among the group.

payload.name: the guests
payload.note: Guests of the royal party, mostly Kings and Queens, in the procession and at the game.

stages.label: the guests

quotes.quote: Next came the guests, mostly Kings and Queens
these were all shaped like the three gardeners, oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners

stages.text: the guests: a group of Kings and Queens of the royal party, drawn as flat oblong cards with heads, arms and legs, hands and feet at the corners, in the pattern of the pack. Each wears a Victorian-style robe and a small crown or royal headdress, with rich colours and ermine-like trim. Among them moves the White Rabbit, an animal with a rabbit's face, human posture and a waistcoat, though he is a separate figure and not part of this group's canon.

payload.name: The Queen's croquet-ground
payload.note: The Queen's croquet-ground (also called the croquet ground or croquet lawn), a ridged and furrowed field where the Queen's croquet game and executions take place; both entries describe this same single place.

stages.label: The Queen's croquet-ground

quotes.quote: it was all ridges and furrows
the soldiers had to double themselves up and to stand on their hands and feet, to make the arches
all the arches are gone from this side of the ground

stages.text: The Queen's croquet-ground: a wide lawn in the Queen's garden, its surface broken into long ridges and furrows that make the turf uneven underfoot. Tall hedges and a few shady trees border the field, with a distant tree in one corner. Short grass grows between the ridges, and some patches are bare earth. Arches are formed by bent-over card soldiers standing on hands and feet, and wide garden paths lead off to the edges of the ground.

payload.title: The Jury Upset and the King's First Questions

payload.name: The Knave of Hearts
payload.note: The single Knave of Hearts of Wonderland, who carries the King's crown at the croquet ground, is later the chained prisoner accused of stealing the tarts; all three entries are one character, distinguished only by section.

stages.label: The Knave of Hearts

quotes.quote: these were ornamented all over with diamonds
Then followed the Knave of Hearts, carrying the King’s crown on a crimson velvet cushion
the Knave was standing before them, in chains, with a soldier on each side to guard him
(Which he certainly did _not_, being made entirely of cardboard.)

stages.text: The Knave of Hearts: a flat, oblong card courtier of the Queen's pack, drawn as a card with a head, arms and legs and no human body beneath, made of stiff cardboard. He is an adult figure of the pack, with a small round head and simple face, his card tunic printed with red hearts. He wears a plain tunic patterned with red hearts and carries the King's crown on a crimson velvet cushion. When brought to trial he is shackled in chains.

payload.name: Bill the Lizard
payload.note: The one lizard named Bill, first sent down the chimney by the Rabbit's servants and later a juror in the jury box whose pencil is stolen and who writes on a slate; all three entries describe this same lizard across divisions.

stages.label: Bill the Lizard

quotes.quote: The poor little Lizard, Bill, was in the middle, being held up by two guinea-pigs
the poor little juror (it was Bill, the Lizard) could not make out at all what had become of it
she had put the Lizard in head downwards, and the poor little thing was waving its tail about

stages.text: Bill the Lizard: a small, slender lizard with a lizard's face, scaled green-brown skin and a long tail, standing upright in human posture and dressed in a Victorian waistcoat and small hat, a juror's slate and pencil in hand. Thin-limbed and modest in size, with a narrow sloping snout and bright eyes. Signature prop: a slate and slate-pencil, the pencil often squeaking.

payload.name: The Jury
payload.note: The twelve bird and beast creatures who sit in the jury box, write on slates and tumble out during the trial; both divisions describe this same collective body, so it is one cluster.

stages.label: The Jury

quotes.quote: those twelve creatures
some of them were animals, and some were birds
The twelve jurors were all writing very busily on slates.
upsetting all the jurymen on to the heads of the crowd below

stages.text: The Jury: a group of twelve creatures, a mix of birds and beasts with animal faces and human posture, each wearing a Victorian waistcoat and a period hat; they sit in a jury box, each holding a slate and pencil, and are small enough to be tipped out and gathered up again.

payload.name: The Court Crowd
payload.note: The spectators of the trial who look at Alice and are upset when the jury box falls; not the little animals and birds gathered at the Rabbit's house.

stages.label: Court Crowd

quotes.quote: upsetting all the jurymen on to the heads of the crowd below

stages.text: The Court Crowd: a loose body of spectators in period Victorian dress, typical member an adult figure in a dark frock coat or long skirt with a plain waistcoat and a top hat or bonnet, mid-adult age range, average build, fair-to-pale skin, hair kept under the hat, heads tipped up toward the trial. Their outfits are muted greys, browns and dark blues. Signature prop: a small folded paper or fan held in one hand, a plain card-stock lapel badge. Ordinary people, not card courtiers, and no animal or bird figures.

aliases: the distance where the trial is beginning
payload.name: The Royal Court of Hearts
payload.note: The royal courtroom where the Knave of Hearts is tried, also called the Court of Hearts or the court of justice; the Lobster Quadrille entry, heard only in the distance as the trial begins, is the same trial and the same court.

stages.label: The Royal Court of Hearts

quotes.quote: The King and Queen of Hearts were seated on their throne when they arrived
In the very middle of the court was a table, with a large dish of tarts upon it
The judge, by the way, was the King
The twelve jurors were all writing very busily on slates.
she had put the Lizard in head downwards
throwing an inkstand at the Lizard as she spoke

stages.text: The Royal Court of Hearts: a crowded royal courtroom in a flat, open hall, with a raised throne where the King and Queen of Hearts sit, a jury-box holding twelve jurors writing on slates, and a central table laden with a large dish of tarts. Standing witness space, guards and a canvas bag used to suppress applause sit near the court. Bunting, banners and heart motifs decorate the walls and throne in a whimsical, slightly unsettling style, with ink spilled across the floor and tables.

payload.title: The Baby Becomes a Pig

payload.name: Baby
payload.note: The Duchess's child, which sneezes and howls, is handed to Alice, and turns into a pig in her arms before she sets it free in the wood.

stages.label: Baby

quotes.quote: a queer-shaped little creature, and held out its arms and legs in all directions
a _very_ turn-up nose, much more like a snout than a real nose; also its eyes were getting extremely small for a baby
it was sneezing and howling alternately without a moment's pause

stages.text: Baby: a very young infant, newborn to a few months old, small and round-bodied with limbs that flail in all directions. Skin pale and flushed from sneezing. Little wisps of fine hair on the head. Face with a markedly turned-up nose that is becoming snout-like, and very small eyes. Wears a plain, simple infant's gown or swaddling in pale white or cream cloth, without ornament. No props. Carried by others, never alone.

payload.name: Duchess's House
payload.note: The Duchess's house with its door into a smoky kitchen full of pepper and soup; distinguished from the March Hare's house by its kitchen and the Duchess's household.

stages.label: Duchess's House

quotes.quote: rapped loudly at the door with his knuckles
The door led right into a large kitchen, which was full of smoke from one end to the other
the cook was leaning over the fire, stirring a large cauldron which seemed to be full of soup
There was certainly too much of it in the air.

stages.text: Duchess's House: a small, low house standing at the edge of a wood, with a plain front door set into rough timber and stone walls blackened by soot. Inside, a large kitchen, filled with smoke from one end to the other and thick with pepper in the air, has a wide open hearth with a roaring fire, a heavy cauldron of soup hung over the flames, shelves crowded with pans, plates and dishes, a three-legged wooden stool in the middle of the floor, and fire-irons leaning against the hearth stones. Pots and kettles hang from iron hooks on the walls.

payload.name: the Wood
payload.note: The single wood Alice wanders through across the divisions, including its treetops, the woodland by the Duchess's house, and the tree with the door; no other entry in this group is a separate place.

stages.label: the Wood

quotes.quote: safe in a thick wood
the tops of the trees under which she had been wandering
a footman in livery came running out of the wood

stages.text: The Wood: a dense, shadowed woodland of tall trees whose leafy treetops spread into a canopy far above, with thick undergrowth, a great thistle, clumps of buttercups and grass underfoot, and mushrooms growing at the foot of the trunks. Clearings open here and there, and a small house stands in one of them, with a little door set into a tree trunk nearby.

payload.title: The Hatter's testimony begins

payload.name: The officers of the court
payload.note: Court officers at the trial who suppress the guinea-pigs, fetch lists and remove the Dormouse and the cook; they are separate from the Queen's card soldiers, though the text also says the soldiers guard the Knave, so this link is uncertain.

stages.label: Court officers

quotes.quote: the officers of the court. (As that is rather a hard word
getting the Dormouse turned out, and, by the time they had settled down again, the cook had disappeared.

stages.text: The officers of the court: flat oblong cards with heads, arms and legs, standing in a row at the edges of the courtroom. Each card wears a plain tunic-free card body in the red and white of the Queen's pack, with a small round head, stiff short arms and two legs. They carry a large canvas bag tied with strings and wear no hats or costume beyond the card face markings.

payload.title: The dance and the whiting

payload.name: the Mock Turtle
payload.note: A sad, sobbing creature with a calf's head and tail who tells of his schooldays under the sea and describes the Lobster Quadrille; both entries are the same individual, so there is no other Mock Turtle to tell apart in this group.

stages.label: the Mock Turtle

quotes.quote: Once,” said the Mock Turtle at last, with a deep sigh, “I was a real Turtle.
sitting sad and lonely on a little ledge of rock
in a deep, hollow tone
with tears running down his cheeks

stages.text: The Mock Turtle: an older creature with a calf's head, large tearful eyes, and a calf's tail, body in a Victorian gentleman's waistcoat and coat with a small hat, posed with human stance, flappers for hands. Calm, sad and sobbing, with a deep hollow voice. Sits on a rock ledge under the sea.

payload.name: the Gryphon
payload.note: A single mythical Gryphon (eagle head, lion body) who guides Alice through several chapters, appearing in all three divisions; the same creature in every entry, so no need to split.

stages.label: the Gryphon

quotes.quote: a Gryphon, lying fast asleep in the sun
The Gryphon sat up and rubbed its eyes
it set to work shaking him and punching him in the back

stages.text: the Gryphon: a mythical creature with an eagle's head with a hooked beak and bright eyes, feathered wings folded at its shoulders, and the body of a lion with tawny golden fur and powerful clawed paws. Its feathers are a warm brown and gold, and its fur is a sandy tawny colour.

aliases: the place where the Mock Turtle and Gryphon sit
payload.name: The Gryphon's clearing by the Mock Turtle
payload.note: The unnamed spot where Alice sits with the Mock Turtle and Gryphon and the Lobster Quadrille is danced; the scene's ground in the Mock Turtle sections, not the wood with the little house.

stages.label: Clearing by the sea-shore

quotes.quote: you first form into a line along the sea-shore
They are waiting on the shingle
when you’ve cleared all the jelly-fish out of the way

stages.text: The Gryphon's clearing by the Mock Turtle: a level stretch of pale shingle at the edge of a wide sea in Wonderland, the water a soft grey-green beyond the shore. Scattered jelly-fish lie drying on the stones, and a few low sea-grasses and tufts of wiry shore-weed grow where the sand gives way to shingle. No landmarks mark the spot; the open sea and a distant grey line of cliffs are the only features on the horizon, with no buildings or people in sight.
